events.name: Royal Rumble 2019
events.significance: Seth Rollins's Royal Rumble win in his first attempt, entering #10 and eliminating Braun Strowman after surviving 43:00, the match's longest individual time -- he went on to win the Universal Championship from Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 35. This match is also notable for Nia Jax's historic appearance: a…

notableMoments.title: Seth Rollins wins the Royal Rumble in his first attempt
notableMoments.description: Rollins entered #10 and won by eliminating Braun Strowman, surviving 43:00 (the match's longest individual time), earning a Universal Championship match against Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 35 -- which he won, becoming Universal Champion.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax becomes the first person to compete in both Royal Rumble matches on the same night
notableMoments.description: Nia Jax, a Women's-division wrestler, attacked advertised #30 entrant R-Truth on the ramp before he could enter and took his spot in the Men's Royal Rumble -- becoming the first person to compete in both the men's and women's Rumble matches on the same card, and the first to score an elimination in both (eliminating Mustafa Ali here; see build_2019_women.py for her women's-match appearance). Per Jerry Lawler's own podcast account, the scripted attack legitimately hurt R-Truth (ankle and face).

notableMoments.title: The Mustafa Ali/Nia Jax elimination spot was originally meant for someone else
notableMoments.description: Per Mustafa Ali's own later interview, the spot in which Nia Jax eliminated him was originally designed for a different, unnamed wrestler who declined it, uncomfortable being eliminated by a woman. Ali volunteered as the replacement, reportedly at Jamie Noble's request. This is a separate matter from Nia Jax's legitimate injuring of R-Truth earlier in the same match (see NM066) -- Ali later suffered an unrelated concussion at a house show in February 2019, not connected to the Rumble.

notableMoments.title: Braun Strowman led all eliminators, with a disputed exact total
notableMoments.description: Braun Strowman was widely reported as having the most eliminations of the match. A literal box-score walk of the table gives him 6 (4 solo -- Shelton Benjamin, Baron Corbin, Andrade, Dolph Ziggler -- plus shared credits on Jeff Hardy and Drew McIntyre); Fightful.com's own published stats article instead states 5, likely not crediting him on the McIntyre spot. See flags.csv F381.

notableMoments.title: Shinsuke Nakamura won the United States Championship hours before entering the Rumble
notableMoments.description: Nakamura defeated Rusev to win the United States Championship on the Kickoff Show, then entered the Men's Royal Rumble at #3 as reigning champion -- the only confirmed Rumble entrant who also wrestled earlier on the same card.

notableMoments.title: Two reigning NXT/NXT UK champions entered as surprise call-ups
notableMoments.description: Johnny Gargano entered #6 as reigning NXT North American Champion (won from Ricochet the night before at NXT TakeOver: Phoenix); Pete Dunne entered #18 as reigning NXT UK Champion (a reign stretching back to May 2017). Neither title was on the line in this non-title match.

notableMoments.title: Ziggler/McIntyre Rumble spot paid off their late-2018 tag team split
notableMoments.description: Drew McIntyre and Dolph Ziggler had been a Raw Tag Team Championship-winning duo (won Sept 3, 2018) who lost the titles Oct 22, 2018 and split in December 2018 after a steel cage match. Ziggler eliminated McIntyre from this Rumble by launching him over Braun Strowman's back, a storyline payoff of that feud -- neither man held a title at the time.

notableMoments.title: Cena pulled with legit ankle injury, replaced by Strowman
notableMoments.description: John Cena suffered a left ankle injury on the January 14, 2019 Raw when Drew McIntyre trapped him in an ankle lock during a Fatal 4-Way with Finn Bálor and Baron Corbin. He couldn't recover in time and was pulled from the Men's Royal Rumble; Braun Strowman was announced as his replacement on January 21, six days before the event.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax's men's Rumble cameo was Johnny Laurinaitis's idea to "spice up" the match
notableMoments.description: Nia Jax later said the plan to have her enter the Men's Royal Rumble (after being eliminated from the women's match) came from Johnny Laurinaitis, who pitched it to Vince McMahon. "I think they were just wanting to spice up [the match], make it different," Jax said, adding that McMahon enthusiastically approved it and that she was happy to go along with whatever McMahon proposed.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax becomes only wrestler to compete in both Rumbles same night in 2019
notableMoments.description: After being eliminated near-last from the Women's Royal Rumble, Nia Jax attacked #30 entrant R-Truth and took his spot in the Men's Royal Rumble — making her the only wrestler to compete in both the men's and women's matches on the same night in 2019 (and, per WWE's own recap, only the fourth woman ever to appear in a Men's Rumble). She eliminated Mustafa Ali before being eliminated by the combined effort of Randy Orton, Rey Mysterio and Dolph Ziggler.

notableMoments.title: Strowman ties his own record for most eliminations, 4th time doing it
notableMoments.description: Braun Strowman recorded 6 eliminations in the 2019 Men's Rumble, described as the fourth time he'd led/matched the field in eliminations in a Rumble appearance — a mark no other superstar has matched more than three times.

notableMoments.title: Brock Lesnar ties the all-time single-Rumble elimination record with 13
notableMoments.description: Entering at #1, Brock Lesnar eliminated 13 opponents in a row (11 solo, plus Keith Lee and Braun Strowman -- see F396) before being eliminated himself by Drew McIntyre after surviving 26:24 -- tying the all-time record for most eliminations by a single competitor in one Royal Rumble match.

notableMoments.title: Drew McIntyre wins his first Royal Rumble
notableMoments.description: McIntyre entered #16 and won by eliminating Roman Reigns with a Claymore Kick, surviving 34:11 (the match's longest individual time). He earned a WWE Championship match of his choosing at WrestleMania 36, which he used to challenge and defeat Brock Lesnar -- the same wrestler he had just eliminated from this Rumble.

notableMoments.title: Edge's surprise in-ring return
notableMoments.description: Edge, retired since 2011 due to a career-threatening neck injury and a WWE Hall of Famer, made a surprise in-ring comeback entering #21, surviving 23:43 (the match's 2nd-longest individual time) and eliminating AJ Styles, Luke Gallows and Randy Orton before being eliminated by Roman Reigns. Widely described as the show's marquee angle.

notableMoments.title: Seth Rollins's 'Monday Night Messiah' alliance picks off a brief Owens/Black/Joe trio
notableMoments.description: Kevin Owens, Aleister Black, and Samoa Joe briefly formed their own in-ring alliance before being picked off consecutively by Seth Rollins, who was backed throughout the match by outside interference from Akam and Rezar (Authors of Pain) as part of his heel-authority 'Monday Night Messiah' storyline. Owens, Black, Joe and Rollins's associates brawled to the back together after Rollins's own elimination.

notableMoments.title: Four different championships were represented in the field
notableMoments.description: This match featured 5 reigning champions across 4 titles: Brock Lesnar (WWE Championship), Kofi Kingston & Big E (SmackDown Tag Team Championship, as a duo), Shinsuke Nakamura (Intercontinental Championship), and Keith Lee (NXT North American Championship, won just 4 days earlier). None of these titles were defended within the match itself.

notableMoments.title: Lashley and Rusev pulled after "parking lot brawl," several others missing from the field
notableMoments.description: Bobby Lashley and Rusev were advertised for the Men's Rumble but were reported (in a storyline framed by commentator Michael Cole) as "not cleared to compete" after a brawl in the parking lot earlier that day, tied to their ongoing Lana-driven feud. Buddy Murphy, Otis, Tucker and R-Truth were also advertised for the men's match but did not appear in it — Murphy instead aligned with AOP against Seth Rollins, and Otis/Tucker were redirected into the Women's Rumble angle instead.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns learned of Kobe Bryant's death backstage from Triple H right before the show
notableMoments.description: Reigns found out about Kobe Bryant and Gianna Bryant's deaths at Minute Maid Park just before the event when Triple H showed him a text message. He said: "I never really thought losing someone like that...would affect me so much. It really did," and described going straight to his sleeping daughter's room to hold her after flying home that night.

notableMoments.title: Drew McIntyre dedicated his Rumble win to Kobe Bryant
notableMoments.description: After winning the Men's Royal Rumble the same day Kobe Bryant and his daughter died in a helicopter crash, Drew McIntyre publicly paid tribute to them, referencing the tragedy in a post-match social media post.

notableMoments.title: Reigns sets all-time record for most Royal Rumble runner-up finishes (4th time)
notableMoments.description: Eliminated last by winner Drew McIntyre, Roman Reigns finished runner-up in the Men's Rumble for the fourth time in six career appearances (2014, 2017, 2018, 2020), breaking his own record of three set in 2018 — no other wrestler has more than two runner-up finishes.

notableMoments.title: Lesnar ties all-time record with 13 straight eliminations before McIntyre ends his run
notableMoments.description: Entering the match as champion, Brock Lesnar eliminated 13 consecutive wrestlers (Elias, Erick Rowan, Robert Roode, John Morrison, Rey Mysterio, Big E, Kofi Kingston, Cesaro, Shelton Benjamin, Shinsuke Nakamura, MVP, Keith Lee and Braun Strowman), tying the all-time single-match elimination record, before Drew McIntyre eliminated him with a Claymore Kick at the 26:24 mark.

notableMoments.title: Edge wins from the No. 1 entry
notableMoments.description: Edge entered at No. 1 and won the 2021 Men's Royal Rumble, lasting WWE's official 58:27 and last eliminating Randy Orton.

notableMoments.title: The first two entrants become the final two
notableMoments.description: Edge and Randy Orton entered first and second and ultimately became the final two, after Orton spent much of the match outside the ring following the opening injury angle without being eliminated.

notableMoments.title: Christian returns for his first true match since 2014
notableMoments.description: Christian entered at No. 24 in a surprise return, reunited with Edge in the ring, reached the final four and lasted WWE's official 18:12.

notableMoments.title: Non-entrant Omos eliminates Big E and Rey Mysterio
notableMoments.description: Omos, who was at ringside with AJ Styles but was not an official entrant, was officially credited by WWE with eliminating Big E and Rey Mysterio.

notableMoments.title: Keith Lee pulled from Rumble plans after Mia Yim's COVID-19 positive test
notableMoments.description: Mia Yim tested positive for COVID-19 ahead of the show; her real-life partner Keith Lee was consequently held out under WWE's COVID protocols even though his own test status was unclear. Former WWE writer Vince Russo said WWE "had bigger plans for him and to have a run in there" in the Rumble — Lee had reportedly been floated as a possible winner before Vince McMahon rejected the idea as premature — and Big E emerged as an alternative favorite for the win instead.

notableMoments.title: At least three wrestlers pulled from the Rumble card after COVID-19 tests, only one named
notableMoments.description: Per Dave Meltzer's Wrestling Observer Newsletter, "there were at least three people scheduled originally who had to be pulled due to testing positive" for COVID-19 ahead of the show; Mia Yim was the only one who publicly disclosed her positive test, the other two/more were never identified in reporting.

notableMoments.title: Rumble plans were reshuffled late — Ricochet's late-entry pitch scrapped, Roode pulled entirely
notableMoments.description: Ricochet was reportedly originally pitched to enter late in the match but instead entered at #12 (lasting ~12 minutes before Kane eliminated him). Separately, Robert Roode was originally scheduled for the Rumble but was pulled for an unstated reason. A planned RETRIBUTION ringside-interference angle was also scrapped and replaced with a similar spot involving Omos.

notableMoments.title: Edge wins from #1 a decade after his first win, 2nd-oldest winner ever
notableMoments.description: Edge won the Men's Royal Rumble entering at #1 (lasting 58:28), becoming the third wrestler ever to win from the #1 spot after Shawn Michaels (1995) and Chris Benoit (2004). At 47 years old, he became the second-oldest Rumble winner ever behind only Vince McMahon (53, 1999), and did so 11 years after his first win in 2010.

notableMoments.title: Brock Lesnar wins from No. 30
notableMoments.description: Lesnar entered at No. 30 and won after five eliminations.

notableMoments.title: Bad Bunny returns
notableMoments.description: Bad Bunny returned as a surprise celebrity entrant and recorded two eliminations.

notableMoments.title: Johnny Knoxville enters
notableMoments.description: Johnny Knoxville entered at No. 9 and was eliminated by Sami Zayn.

notableMoments.title: Omos group elimination
notableMoments.description: Six official entrants combined to eliminate Omos.

notableMoments.title: Shane McMahon's entrance mixed up with Randy Orton's, sparking his firing
notableMoments.description: Shane McMahon (who was also producing the match) and Randy Orton had their entrance order mixed up on the night — accounts vary on the exact mechanics (a genuine music/graphics mix-up vs. Orton reportedly refusing to enter to McMahon's music), but all agree McMahon ended up entering to the wrong cue, visibly frustrated, while Orton found it hilarious backstage, laughing and (per his own later comment) "rolling on the floor." McMahon lasted about five minutes before Brock Lesnar eliminated him. Orton joked afterward: "Shane McMahon got axed after that... Sorry Shane, love you man." Vince McMahon reportedly fired Shane days later, telling him he'd "never get another pop in this company" as long as Vince was around.

notableMoments.title: Chaotic, last-minute-change-filled production; WrestleMania sign caught fire twice
notableMoments.description: An in-depth insider report described the 2022 Men's Rumble as one of the most "frustrating and stressful" experiences of several talents' careers, with changes to who-eliminates-whom happening right up until wrestlers entered the ring. The WrestleMania sign at the venue caught fire twice due to pyrotechnics malfunctions, forcing evacuations that disrupted the show.

notableMoments.title: Kofi Kingston's signature save spot finally fails him
notableMoments.description: Kingston attempted his signature top-rope-save spot, but after Kevin Owens shoved him toward the barricade, both of his feet touched the floor, resulting in his elimination and ending his long streak of successful creative saves. Kingston himself acknowledged it afterward: "You're bound to mess one up, that's just the way things go."

notableMoments.title: Lesnar's 2022 win set several speed/gap records
notableMoments.description: Winning from the #30 spot in 2:30, Brock Lesnar reportedly set the record for fastest Royal Rumble win ever (beating Edge's 2010 mark by over 5 minutes), became a two-time winner with a 19-year gap between victories (2003 to 2022) — the longest gap between wins by any two-time winner — and was the fourth person ever to win from the #30 spot.

notableMoments.title: Cesaro was backstage at the event but did not appear in the Rumble
notableMoments.description: Cesaro was present backstage at the 2022 Royal Rumble, and many fans had hoped to see him enter the Men's Rumble match, but he was not used in it.

notableMoments.title: Gunther lasts 71:40
notableMoments.description: Gunther entered No. 1 and survived 1:11:40, reaching the final two.

notableMoments.title: Rey Mysterio does not appear
notableMoments.description: Mysterio was assigned No. 17 but never appeared or entered the ring.

notableMoments.title: Ricochet and Logan Paul collide
notableMoments.description: Ricochet and Logan Paul launched from opposite sides and collided in mid-air.

notableMoments.title: Rey Mysterio pulled with injury, Dominik enters in his place
notableMoments.description: Rey Mysterio was advertised for the No. 17 slot but never appeared after suffering an injury during a SmackDown match against Karrion Kross the night before (Jan 27, 2023) in Laredo, TX — a match he actually won despite the injury. After his entrance music played and roughly 90 seconds passed with no Rey, his son Dominik emerged at No. 18 instead, tearing up one of his father's masks; Dominik lasted over 25 minutes before eventual winner Cody Rhodes eliminated him.

notableMoments.title: Kofi Kingston mistimes near-elimination spot, crashes into announce table
notableMoments.description: During the men's Rumble, Kofi Kingston mistimed a signature "save himself from elimination" spot and ended up crashing into the announce table rather than landing cleanly, though he was not counted out and continued in the match.

notableMoments.title: Gunther breaks Rey Mysterio's 17-year Iron Man record entering at #1
notableMoments.description: Entering first, Gunther lasted 1 hour, 11 minutes and 25 seconds, surpassing Rey Mysterio's 2006 record of 1:02:12 by roughly nine minutes. He also tied Cody Rhodes for most eliminations in the match with five, dispatching opponents including Drew McIntyre, Sheamus and Booker T.

notableMoments.title: Entry #30 becomes the winningest slot; Corbin's blink-and-miss-it run; Miz's odd double
notableMoments.description: Cody Rhodes' win from the #30 slot made it the most successful entry position in Rumble history (5 winners, surpassing #27's 4). The same match saw Baron Corbin eliminated in under 10 seconds — the shortest men's run of the night — while The Miz was cited as only the second wrestler, after Santino Marella, to be eliminated in exactly two different Royal Rumble matches.

notableMoments.title: Producers, runtime and gate behind the Jan. 28, 2023 show
notableMoments.description: Fightful reported the men's Rumble was produced by Michael Hayes, Shane Helms, Jason Jordan, Kenny Dykstra and Jamie Noble. The show ran about 12 minutes over its scheduled 4-hour slot, and the live gate topped $7.7 million with sponsorship revenue roughly double prior Rumbles.

notableMoments.title: Owens' moonsault mistimed on "slippery" ropes in the undercard title match
notableMoments.description: In the Roman Reigns–Kevin Owens Undisputed Title match on the same card, Owens' jumping moonsault off the top rope was mistimed — he lost his footing on ropes he described as "a little slippery" and fell onto Reigns rather than connecting cleanly.

notableMoments.description: McAfee left commentary for entry 22, entered the ring and jumped out.

notableMoments.title: CM Punk suffers a triceps injury
notableMoments.description: Punk reached the final two; on the following Raw he disclosed a triceps injury sustained in the Rumble.

notableMoments.title: Brock Lesnar pulled over Janel Grant lawsuit allegations, Breakker inserted late
notableMoments.description: Lesnar, advertised as a surprise entrant, was pulled from the card in the days before the event after being referenced in the Janel Grant lawsuit against Vince McMahon, WWE and John Laurinaitis (as reported by the Wall Street Journal). Bron Breakker was hastily inserted in his place at #20, essentially running Lesnar's planned spot — per Dave Meltzer, Breakker "threw out the guys" Lesnar was scheduled to eliminate (Omos, Ivar, Finn Balor, Jimmy Uso) and "got thrown out exactly how Brock Lesnar was going to," lasting just over five minutes before Dominik Mysterio eliminated him.

notableMoments.title: CM Punk tears his triceps taking McIntyre's Future Shock DDT
notableMoments.description: CM Punk suffered a torn triceps during the match while taking Drew McIntyre's Future Shock DDT, forcing him out of his advertised WrestleMania XL program. Punk later described the moment on WWE Playback: "My world comes crashing down. Instantly I knew I tore my tricep. There was about a silver dollar hole in my tricep that I instantly sunk two fingers into so I knew it was gone." He finished the match before the injury was publicly confirmed two days later.

notableMoments.title: Vince McMahon resigns from TKO one day before the show
notableMoments.description: Vince McMahon resigned from TKO's board and all WWE positions on January 26, 2024 — one day before the Royal Rumble — following the Janel Grant lawsuit, casting a real-world shadow over a show his own advertised return (Lesnar) had already been pulled from.

notableMoments.title: Rhodes becomes first back-to-back winner since "Stone Cold" (1997–98)
notableMoments.description: Cody Rhodes' 2024 win made him the first wrestler to win consecutive Royal Rumble matches since Steve Austin's back-to-back victories in 1997 and 1998.

notableMoments.title: Gunther's day-mix-up on Raw forces WWE to scramble a correction graphic
notableMoments.description: On the January 22, 2024 Raw, Gunther told the crowd he'd win the Royal Rumble "this Sunday" — the event was actually the following Saturday, January 27. Per Fightful Select (as relayed by WrestleTalk), WWE "scrambled to put up a 'Royal Rumble this Saturday' graphic," and Michael Cole repeatedly corrected the date on commentary. Gunther later joked on social media that he meant "this Sunday 2am CET," which converts to Saturday 8pm ET in the US.

notableMoments.description: Independent timing80:10 exceeds the2018 Greatest Royal Rumble; duration disagreement flagged.

notableMoments.title: Penta early floor-contact dispute
notableMoments.description: Independent analysis questions an early apparent two-foot contact; no official elimination was ruled, so retain later Finn Balor elimination.

notableMoments.title: Rollins attacks Reigns after elimination
notableMoments.description: Punk eliminated Rollins and Reigns; Rollins attacked Reigns afterward.

notableMoments.title: Tozawa "attacked" by Carmelo Hayes pre-entrance, IShowSpeed steps in at #8
notableMoments.description: Advertised entrant Akira Tozawa was attacked by Carmelo Hayes upon entering and was carried to the back, ruled unable to compete; streamer/rapper IShowSpeed was inserted in his place at #8.

notableMoments.title: Jey Uso's win called one of the biggest upsets in Royal Rumble history
notableMoments.description: Jey Uso won by eliminating John Cena in the final two, a result Forbes called "perhaps the biggest upset in Royal Rumble history," earning Uso a surprise WrestleMania 41 main-event slot.

notableMoments.title: AJ Styles returns from a months-long injury layoff at #21
notableMoments.description: AJ Styles returned as the #21 entrant after being out since October 2024 with injury; he was ultimately eliminated by Logan Paul (#30).

notableMoments.title: Cena's #23 entrance draws "the pop of the night" in his farewell Rumble
notableMoments.description: John Cena's entrance at #23 — during his retirement tour — reportedly drew the loudest crowd reaction ("the pop of the night") of the match.

notableMoments.title: Reigns/Rollins/Punk triangle plays out mid-match, foreshadowing WrestleMania build
notableMoments.description: During the match, Seth Rollins delivered a Stomp to Roman Reigns on the steel steps outside the ring, and CM Punk's entrance at #25 created a three-way staredown between Punk, Reigns and Rollins — an in-match angle used to set up the Reigns/Rollins/Punk WrestleMania 41 triangle.

notableMoments.description: Former Powerhouse Hobbs entered at14 under his new ring name.

notableMoments.title: Both El Grande Americanos collide
notableMoments.description: Returning original masked wrestler eliminated the second incarnation.

notableMoments.title: Masked attack precedes Breakker elimination
notableMoments.description: An unidentified masked attacker assaulted Breakker before he entered; Femi then eliminated him first. No attacker identity guessed.

notableMoments.title: Nonentrant McIntyre eliminates Rhodes
notableMoments.description: WWE explicitly assigns the outside-interference elimination to McIntyre.

notableMoments.title: Reigns wins his second Royal Rumble
notableMoments.description: Reigns last eliminated Gunther, adding to his2015 victory.

notableMoments.title: Masked assailant (widely assumed Seth Rollins) ambushes Bron Breakker pre-match; he's eliminated almost immediately
notableMoments.description: Before entering the match, Bron Breakker was attacked by a hooded/masked assailant who escaped into the crowd; recaps describe the attacker as "assumed to be" or "revealed to be" Seth Rollins. Breakker nonetheless entered the Rumble but was eliminated almost immediately by Oba Femi, with the angle drawing real-feeling controversy involving Paul Heyman.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns becomes the 12th two-time Royal Rumble winner
notableMoments.description: Reigns' win (his first since 2015) made him the 12th wrestler to win multiple Royal Rumble matches.

notableMoments.title: Brock Lesnar's final Royal Rumble appearance, on his retirement tour
notableMoments.description: Brock Lesnar entered at #22 in what was reported as his final Royal Rumble appearance before retirement — a farewell nod to a wrestler who had previously won the 2003 and 2022 Rumbles.

notableMoments.title: Riyadh show was WWE's 14th Saudi event and first "Big Five" show there
notableMoments.description: The 2026 Royal Rumble — the first traditional Royal Rumble held outside North America — was reported as WWE's 14th event in Saudi Arabia and the first of the company's "Big Five" annual premium live events to be held there, tied to WWE's long-term partnership with Saudi Vision 2030.

notableMoments.title: NXT call-up Oba Femi opens the match at #1 and nearly steals the show
notableMoments.description: Oba Femi entered #1 in his main-roster Rumble debut and recorded five eliminations — one recap compared his dominant opening stretch to "Brock [Lesnar] in 2020" — before eventually being eliminated by the real Brock Lesnar.

notableMoments.title: "Original El Grande Americano" gimmick teases a Finn Balor reveal that never comes
notableMoments.description: Chad Gable returned under the masked "Original El Grande Americano" gimmick; a mid-match close-up of a newly grown goatee briefly fueled fan speculation he might actually be Finn Balor, before the dual-Americano angle ended when Trick Williams eliminated both masked wrestlers.

notableMoments.title: Kane's then-record 8th consecutive Royal Rumble appearance -- PROBABLE, not CONFIRMED
notableMoments.description: Per a single independent stats-blog source (Rumblemetrics), Kane's 2006 entry marked his then-record 8th consecutive Royal Rumble appearance. Not independently cross-checked against a second source this pass, so logged here at PROBABLE rather than CONFIRMED -- a deliberate example of this database surfacing an interesting single-sourced claim honestly rather than silently upgrading its confidence.

notableMoments.title: Drew Carey's Rumble spot began as an act of retaliation
notableMoments.description: Comedian Drew Carey became the first celebrity entrant in Royal Rumble history, entering at #5. According to reporting, Vince McMahon put him in the match after misreading a conversation between Carey and Trish Stratus, essentially as payback, hoping Carey would get roughed up on camera. Carey eliminated himself by climbing over the top rope to escape Kane.

notableMoments.title: Kane sets a new single-match elimination record
notableMoments.description: Kane eliminated 11 wrestlers in the 2001 Rumble, breaking the previous elimination record of 10 (shared by Hulk Hogan in 1989 and Steve Austin in 1997) and also logging the match's longest individual time at 53:46. His mark stood until Roman Reigns eliminated 12 wrestlers in 2014.

notableMoments.title: Spike Dudley never enters after Kane's ramp attack
notableMoments.description: Spike Dudley was announced for the #13 slot, but Undertaker's gong-style music played as a ruse and Kane instead attacked Dudley on the entrance ramp with a chokeslam before he could reach the ring, meaning he was credited as an entrant but never actually competed.

notableMoments.title: Kane sets new consecutive-appearances record
notableMoments.description: Kane's 2006 Rumble appearance was his 8th consecutive year in the match (1999–2006), breaking the prior record of 7 straight appearances that had been shared by Rick Martel, Owen Hart, and Kane himself.

notableMoments.title: Santino sets the record for fastest Rumble elimination
notableMoments.description: Santino Marella entered at #28 and was eliminated by Kane in roughly 1-1.5 seconds (WWE's own video title says "one second"), breaking the previous record of 2 seconds held by The Warlord — the fastest elimination in Royal Rumble history.

notableMoments.title: Santino's own explanation for the instant elimination
notableMoments.description: Santino Marella has claimed the reason Kane blasted him immediately was a backstage grudge over a piece of chicken they'd both gone for in catering — a story he has told as a joke in interviews, with no confirmation it reflects the real booking reason.

notableMoments.title: Kane ties his own Rumble appearance record
notableMoments.description: Kane's 2010 Rumble appearance was his 12th overall, tying Shawn Michaels' then-record for most career Royal Rumble appearances.

notableMoments.title: Kane set records for both total Rumble matches worked and consecutive events attended
notableMoments.description: The 2015 Royal Rumble was Kane's 18th Royal Rumble match, a company record, and his 20th consecutive Royal Rumble event in some capacity (wrestler or otherwise) dating back to 1996.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns's broadcast-record 12 eliminations sparked a fan backlash when Batista won
notableMoments.description: Reigns, in his Rumble debut, was broadcast-credited with a Rumble-record 12 eliminations and was the clear live-crowd favorite, while Batista -- a part-time returning veteran -- was booed heavily for winning instead, in a moment that sparked a well-known, lasting fan backlash. This database's own guest-analyst source recalculates Reigns's total at 9.5 under an even-split partial-credit system for shared eliminations (see F277); that recalculation remains single-sourced and has not been corroborated by any other source checked, so it is noted here honestly rather than adopted as a second confirmed figure.

notableMoments.title: Daniel Bryan's early elimination sparked heavy boos for Roman Reigns's win in Philadelphia
notableMoments.description: Reigns's win, entering at #19 and eliminating Rusev in the match's final moments, was met with heavy boos from the live Philadelphia crowd, still upset over Daniel Bryan's comparatively early elimination (10:11 survival, only the 10th-longest of the match). A surprise late appearance from The Rock, endorsing Reigns and physically confronting the already-eliminated Big Show and Kane, did not turn the crowd.

notableMoments.title: The WWE Championship was defended -- and lost -- inside the Rumble match itself
notableMoments.description: Roman Reigns, the reigning WWE Champion, entered at #1 and defended the title WITHIN the match itself, only the second time in Royal Rumble history a world title was decided by the match itself (after Ric Flair in 1992). He lost the title when Triple H won the match, becoming WWE Champion by winning the Rumble.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns wrestled twice in one night -- losing the Universal Championship, then nearly winning the Rumble
notableMoments.description: Reigns lost the WWE Universal Championship to Kevin Owens in a No Disqualification match earlier the same card (with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage above the ring), then entered the Royal Rumble at #30, eliminated The Undertaker, and made the final two before losing to Randy Orton.

notableMoments.title: Rollins attacks Reigns after elimination
notableMoments.description: Punk eliminated Rollins and Reigns; Rollins attacked Reigns afterward.

notableMoments.title: Reigns wins his second Royal Rumble
notableMoments.description: Reigns last eliminated Gunther, adding to his2015 victory.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns set a new single-Rumble elimination record with 12
notableMoments.description: Roman Reigns eliminated 12 competitors during the 2014 Royal Rumble, breaking Kane's previous record of 11 eliminations in a single match (set in 2001).

notableMoments.title: Daniel Bryan told WWE beforehand that his fast elimination was a bad idea
notableMoments.description: Returning from neck surgery, Bryan was booked for only 4–5 minutes in the 2015 Rumble. He has since said he personally told WWE management ahead of time, "I think this is a bad idea. This isn't necessarily great for Roman [Reigns]" — warning that a quick Bryan exit would backfire on crowd reception for Reigns, especially after Bryan had already been excluded from the 2014 match. WWE proceeded with the short spot anyway, and the backlash played out largely as Bryan predicted.

notableMoments.title: WWE production missed the reveal shot of AJ Styles' surprise debut
notableMoments.description: When AJ Styles made his surprise WWE debut entering the 2016 Rumble, the broadcast's cameras stayed on Roman Reigns' reaction in the ring instead of cutting to the titantron as Styles' "I Am Phenomenal" graphic and music revealed his identity, so viewers never saw the reveal live. Former WWE VP of Production Mike Mansury later explained the miss came from secrecy: the segment couldn't be rehearsed that afternoon to protect the surprise, and the director on the show "didn't know it was gonna happen," so he wasn't prepared to cut to the graphic.

notableMoments.title: Crowd booed Reigns loudly for eliminating Undertaker, then cheered when Orton eliminated Reigns
notableMoments.description: When Roman Reigns (entering at #30) eliminated The Undertaker to set up their WrestleMania 33 program, the crowd reacted with heavy, sustained boos; the reaction flipped to cheers when Randy Orton later eliminated Reigns from the match en route to Orton's win.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns learned of Kobe Bryant's death backstage from Triple H right before the show
notableMoments.description: Reigns found out about Kobe Bryant and Gianna Bryant's deaths at Minute Maid Park just before the event when Triple H showed him a text message. He said: "I never really thought losing someone like that...would affect me so much. It really did," and described going straight to his sleeping daughter's room to hold her after flying home that night.

notableMoments.title: Reigns sets all-time record for most Royal Rumble runner-up finishes (4th time)
notableMoments.description: Eliminated last by winner Drew McIntyre, Roman Reigns finished runner-up in the Men's Rumble for the fourth time in six career appearances (2014, 2017, 2018, 2020), breaking his own record of three set in 2018 — no other wrestler has more than two runner-up finishes.

notableMoments.title: Owens' moonsault mistimed on "slippery" ropes in the undercard title match
notableMoments.description: In the Roman Reigns–Kevin Owens Undisputed Title match on the same card, Owens' jumping moonsault off the top rope was mistimed — he lost his footing on ropes he described as "a little slippery" and fell onto Reigns rather than connecting cleanly.

notableMoments.title: Reigns/Rollins/Punk triangle plays out mid-match, foreshadowing WrestleMania build
notableMoments.description: During the match, Seth Rollins delivered a Stomp to Roman Reigns on the steel steps outside the ring, and CM Punk's entrance at #25 created a three-way staredown between Punk, Reigns and Rollins — an in-match angle used to set up the Reigns/Rollins/Punk WrestleMania 41 triangle.

notableMoments.title: Roman Reigns becomes the 12th two-time Royal Rumble winner
notableMoments.description: Reigns' win (his first since 2015) made him the 12th wrestler to win multiple Royal Rumble matches.
