events.name: Royal Rumble 2019
events.significance: Becky Lynch's Royal Rumble win, remarkable for coming the same night she lost her own SmackDown Women's Championship match to Asuka -- she was allowed to take injured advertised entrant Lana's vacated #28 slot, entering, in practice, after #30 Carmella had already gone in (see F392), before eliminating Nia Jax and…

notableMoments.title: Becky Lynch wins the Royal Rumble hours after losing her own title match
notableMoments.description: Lynch lost her SmackDown Women's Championship match to Asuka earlier the same card, then was allowed to take injured advertised entrant Lana's vacated #28 slot -- entering, in practice, after #30 Carmella had already gone in. She eliminated Nia Jax and then Charlotte Flair for the winning elimination after surviving 13:20, earning a spot in the WrestleMania 35 winner-take-all triple threat (also featuring Ronda Rousey and Charlotte Flair), which she won -- becoming the first woman to hold both women's titles simultaneously and headlining the first-ever women's WrestleMania main event.

notableMoments.title: Lana's storyline injury opened the door for Becky Lynch
notableMoments.description: Lana was drawn/assigned the #28 slot and came out as that entrant, but a storyline ankle injury -- suffered when Rusev accidentally knocked her off the ring apron during his Kickoff Show US Championship match -- kept her from actually competing. She has no wrestler_id/entrant row in this database, matching this database's precedent for scheduled-but-never-entered wrestlers.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax competed in both Royal Rumble matches the same night
notableMoments.description: Nia Jax entered #29 in this Women's Royal Rumble (eliminating Io Shirai and Natalya solo, plus a shared credit on Bayley, before being eliminated by Becky Lynch) and later the same night appeared as a surprise entrant in the Men's Royal Rumble as well -- becoming the first person to compete in (and score eliminations in) both Rumble matches on one card. See build_2019_men.py's NM066 for the fuller account, including a legitimate in-ring injury she caused there.

notableMoments.title: Mandy Rose eliminated Naomi despite already being eliminated herself
notableMoments.description: A direct Wikipedia footnote confirms Mandy Rose, having already been eliminated moments earlier, reached back into the ring from the floor and pulled Naomi out -- an unusual blown-spot moment that nonetheless stood as her official elimination credit.

notableMoments.title: Natalya's 56:01 was the longest individual women's Royal Rumble survival time to date
notableMoments.description: Natalya entered #2 and survived 56:01, the longest individual time in Women's Royal Rumble history at the time -- a record that stood until Bianca Belair broke it in 2021.

notableMoments.title: Charlotte Flair led all eliminators with 5 credited eliminations
notableMoments.description: Charlotte Flair (entered #13, runner-up) eliminated Xia Li, Tamina, Lacey Evans and Carmella solo, plus a shared credit on Bayley's elimination -- the match's highest total, before being eliminated herself by Becky Lynch for the winning elimination.

notableMoments.title: Becky Lynch wardrobe malfunction forces broadcast to cut away
notableMoments.description: During her SmackDown Women's Championship match with Asuka on the same card, Becky Lynch's top came undone after a bump; the broadcast feed cut away for a few seconds and returned showing her adjusting her gear. WWE's delay system was used specifically to keep the moment off the actual air.

notableMoments.title: Becky Lynch first to lose a title match then win the Rumble same night
notableMoments.description: Lynch tapped out to Asuka earlier in the card, then went on to win the Women's Royal Rumble later that night — making her the first wrestler credited with losing a major title match but still winning a Royal Rumble on the same show.

notableMoments.title: Liv Morgan set the women's Rumble record for shortest time ever — 8 seconds
notableMoments.description: Entering at #4, Liv Morgan was eliminated by Natalya in just 8 seconds, the shortest stay in Women's Royal Rumble history at that point.

notableMoments.title: Women's match had roughly 10 uncredited botches, including Lacey Evans's rough main-roster debut
notableMoments.description: A botch-spotting recap counted around 10 mistakes through the Women's Rumble, singling out Lacey Evans (making her main-roster in-ring debut), Mickie James and Billie Kay for noticeable errors, though the specific mistakes weren't itemized individually.

events.name: Royal Rumble 2020
events.significance: Charlotte Flair's first Royal Rumble win, entering #17 and eliminating Shayna Baszler for the win after surviving 27:19. Shayna Baszler and Bianca Belair tied for the most eliminations in Women's Royal Rumble history with 8 apiece, breaking Nia Jax's prior record of 7 (see NM083) -- Belair, making her first…

notableMoments.title: Shayna Baszler and Bianca Belair tie for the most eliminations in Women's Royal Rumble history
notableMoments.description: Both Shayna Baszler (entrant #30, runner-up) and Bianca Belair (entrant #2) recorded 8 credited eliminations apiece, tying for the most eliminations by a single competitor in Women's Royal Rumble history and breaking the prior record of 7, held by Nia Jax (RR2018W).

notableMoments.title: Charlotte Flair wins her first Royal Rumble
notableMoments.description: Charlotte Flair entered #17 and won by eliminating Shayna Baszler after surviving 27:19, becoming the first Royal Rumble winner in this database's separate RR2020W record. Her post-match promo was described by contemporary recaps as tonally ambiguous, neither clearly face nor heel.

notableMoments.title: Santino Marella returns as 'Santina' for a comedic self-elimination
notableMoments.description: Santino Marella returned in his 'Santina' drag persona at #29 and eliminated himself using his own 'Cobra' sock-puppet finishing move on himself -- confirmed by 2+ independent sources.

notableMoments.title: Kairi Sane entered as a reigning champion, correcting an initial working assumption
notableMoments.description: Kairi Sane entered #11 as reigning WWE Women's Tag Team Champion alongside Asuka (The Kabuki Warriors, won Oct 6, 2019) -- not Alexa Bliss and Nikki Cross, who did not win the titles until WrestleMania 36 months later, an assumption corrected during this build's research. See F404.

notableMoments.title: Otis 'saves' Mandy Rose in a storyline interference spot
notableMoments.description: Earlier in the match, Mandy Rose was saved from apparent elimination by Otis in a storyline spot connected to the Fire & Desire/Heavy Machinery angle -- praised across multiple contemporary recaps as a standout moment.

notableMoments.title: Beth Phoenix busted open her head on the ring post
notableMoments.description: During a corner exchange with Bianca Belair, Phoenix threw her head back to sell a strike and struck the back of her head on the ring post, opening a cut. Dave Meltzer confirmed on air/in reporting that "Beth Phoenix hit the back of her head on the post so that's where all the blood was coming from." She continued wrestling while bleeding until being eliminated by Shayna Baszler near the end of the match.

notableMoments.title: Otis hid under the ring for roughly five entrances to save Mandy Rose
notableMoments.description: Otis later revealed he was hiding underneath the ring for about five entrances, watching a monitor for his cue, before bursting out to catch Mandy Rose when Alexa Bliss threw her over the top rope. "Probably about five entrances," he said, and joked about the physical challenge of staying concealed that long: "It's funny because they just know it's you in a black cape. You can't hide me."

notableMoments.title: Belair and Baszler share the record for most eliminations in a Women's Rumble (8 each)
notableMoments.description: Bianca Belair (entering at #1) and Shayna Baszler (entering at #30) each recorded 8 eliminations, combining for 16 — over half the 30-woman field — and breaking Nia Jax's previous record of 7.

notableMoments.title: Charlotte Flair becomes first Rumble winner to choose an NXT title shot
notableMoments.description: After winning the Women's Royal Rumble, Charlotte Flair chose to challenge for the NXT Women's Championship at WrestleMania rather than a main-roster title — reportedly the first time a Rumble winner opted for an NXT title opportunity.

events.significance: Bianca Belair won from entry No. 3; WWE described her 56-plus-minute performance as a women’s Royal Rumble longevity record at the time.

notableMoments.title: Bianca Belair wins from No. 3
notableMoments.description: Bianca Belair entered at No. 3 and won, with WWE listing 56:52 of survival time.

notableMoments.title: Rhea Ripley records seven eliminations
notableMoments.description: WWE credits Rhea Ripley with a match-high seven eliminations.

notableMoments.title: Alicia Fox briefly wins the 24/7 Championship
notableMoments.description: During the Royal Rumble, Alicia Fox pinned R-Truth to win the 24/7 Championship before Truth regained it moments later.

notableMoments.title: Official Carmella eliminator credit differs by source
notableMoments.description: WWE lists Tamina as Carmella’s eliminator before Tamina entered the match, while Cagematch lists Reginald; the structured elimination follows WWE’s higher-tier official result.

notableMoments.title: Bayley's elimination came earlier than rehearsed, and cameras missed it live
notableMoments.description: Entering at #1, Bayley was eliminated by eventual winner Bianca Belair around the 29-30 minute mark — but per PWInsider's Mike Johnson, "Bayley's elimination from the match came slightly earlier than had been planned during rehearsals." The live broadcast missed capturing it entirely because cameras were focused on Torrie Wilson's simultaneous elimination on the other side of the ring; producers had to show it via replay afterward.

notableMoments.title: Bianca Belair sets the all-time women's Rumble individual time record
notableMoments.description: Winning from the #3 spot, Bianca Belair lasted 56 minutes 52 seconds (sometimes cited as 56:49), the longest individual performance in Women's Royal Rumble history.

notableMoments.title: Carmella and Alexa Bliss suffered the match's quickest eliminations
notableMoments.description: Carmella was eliminated in just 45 seconds and Alexa Bliss lasted only 1:02 — the two shortest stays of the 2021 Women's Royal Rumble.

notableMoments.title: Two legends made long-awaited Rumble returns
notableMoments.description: The 2021 Women's Rumble featured six NXT call-ups plus four WWE legends, including Victoria (making her first Rumble/in-ring appearance since 2009) and Jillian Hall (her first since 2010).

notableMoments.description: Rousey returned at No. 28 and won.

notableMoments.title: Mickie James enters as Impact champion
notableMoments.description: WWE acknowledged Mickie James as reigning Impact Knockouts World Champion.

notableMoments.title: Sonya Deville eliminates Naomi after elimination
notableMoments.description: Deville returned after her own elimination and WWE officially credited her with eliminating Naomi.

notableMoments.title: Mighty Molly surprise return
notableMoments.description: Molly Holly entered under her Mighty Molly presentation.

notableMoments.title: Vince McMahon pitched having Ronda Rousey eliminate all 29 opponents solo
notableMoments.description: Vince McMahon reportedly pushed hard for a plan to have Ronda Rousey eliminate every other entrant by herself in the Women's Royal Rumble, driven by wanting to fully showcase her on her advertised full-time 2022 schedule. A reporter described the vision as "so off the wall" that it contributed to respected producer TJ Wilson (Tyson Kidd) taking a leave of absence heading into the event.

notableMoments.title: At least one women's wrestler turned down a Rumble spot over Tyson Kidd's absence
notableMoments.description: With regular women's-division producer Tyson Kidd (TJ Wilson) away from WWE around this time, at least one female talent reportedly declined an offer to appear in the Women's Royal Rumble specifically because Kidd wasn't producing it. Fit Finlay, Shane Helms, Pat Buck, Michael Hayes and Molly Holly were brought in to fill the producing gap instead.

notableMoments.title: Vince McMahon initially blocked Mickie James from wearing her Impact title on WWE TV
notableMoments.description: Vince McMahon reportedly forbade Mickie James from being shown wearing her Impact Wrestling Knockouts Championship on WWE programming the night of the Rumble. A producer informed him the title's appearance was contractually required, and McMahon reluctantly relented: "fuck it, fine!"

notableMoments.title: Paige was heavily rumored as a surprise entrant but never appeared
notableMoments.description: In the lead-up to Royal Rumble 2022, Paige was widely rumored among insiders to be a surprise entrant in the Women's Rumble. She did not appear, and WWE subsequently allowed her legends contract to expire without a return.

notableMoments.description: Ripley became the first woman to win the Royal Rumble from the No. 1 position.

notableMoments.title: Ripley and Morgan go wire-to-wire
notableMoments.description: The No. 1 and No. 2 entrants became the final two after each lasting more than 61 minutes.

notableMoments.title: Chelsea Green eliminated in five seconds
notableMoments.description: Returning Chelsea Green was eliminated by Ripley after five seconds.

notableMoments.title: Eleven women eliminate Nia Jax
notableMoments.description: WWE's official RR2023W results explicitly state that the other 11 Superstars eliminated Nia Jax, and its Eliminated By table names Asuka, Lacey Evans, Liv Morgan, Michelle McCool, Michin, Nikki Cross, Piper Niven, Raquel Rodriguez, Rhea Ripley, Sonya Deville, and Shotzi. All 11 therefore receive structured assisted-elimination credit.

notableMoments.title: Chelsea Green sets women's Rumble record for shortest survival — 5 seconds
notableMoments.description: Chelsea Green was eliminated by eventual winner Rhea Ripley just five seconds after entering, setting the record for shortest survival time in a Women's Royal Rumble match.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax's music cued early; Riptide spot mistimed on her elimination
notableMoments.description: With roughly seven seconds left on the entry clock, WWE prematurely played Nia Jax's entrance music before her number was up. Later in the match, Jax also mistimed taking Rhea Ripley's Riptide finisher, contributing to her elimination.

notableMoments.title: Ripley and Morgan jointly set the Iron Woman/longevity record; Ripley wins entering at #1
notableMoments.description: Rhea Ripley (winner) and runner-up Liv Morgan both lasted the entire match, jointly setting a new longevity record of 1 hour, 1 minute, 3 seconds and surpassing Bianca Belair's prior mark of just under 57 minutes. Ripley also became the first woman to win the Rumble entering at #1, and pushed her career Rumble-eliminations total to 20, passing Charlotte Flair's previous record of 15.

notableMoments.title: Early Ripley/Brooke mistimed collision; McCool nearly falls off the barricade
notableMoments.description: Early in the women's Rumble, Rhea Ripley and Dana Brooke mistimed a spot and collided awkwardly. Later, Hall of Famer Michelle McCool, making a legends entrance from the crowd, nearly lost her balance and fell off the barricade.

notableMoments.title: Women's Rumble production team and B-Fab's main-roster in-ring debut
notableMoments.description: Fightful reported the women's Rumble was produced by TJ Wilson, Molly Holly, Petey Williams and Jason Jordan. The same show marked B-Fab's first main-roster in-ring match.

notableMoments.title: Bayley sets women's survival record
notableMoments.description: Naomi exceeded the previous mark before Bayley finished with the official 63:03 record.

notableMoments.title: Jade Cargill's first WWE match
notableMoments.description: Cargill entered at 28 and eliminated Jax.

notableMoments.title: R-Truth mistakes the women's Rumble for his match
notableMoments.description: Truth's interruption preceded Valhalla's entry; he was not an official competitor.

notableMoments.title: Valhalla lasts five seconds
notableMoments.description: Her official five-second duration matched Chelsea Green's 2023 low.

notableMoments.title: TNA champion crosses into WWE
notableMoments.description: Grace entered while holding the TNA Knockouts World Championship.

notableMoments.title: Jade Cargill's in-ring WWE debut — eliminates Nia Jax almost immediately
notableMoments.description: Jade Cargill made her official WWE in-ring debut as a surprise entrant at #28, eliminating the dominant Nia Jax almost as soon as she entered, then had a widely-praised staredown with Bianca Belair.

notableMoments.title: Bayley sets new Iron Woman record, briefly eclipsing Naomi's short-lived mark
notableMoments.description: Naomi broke the 2023 longevity record mid-match at roughly 62:18, only for winner Bayley to break it again minutes later at roughly 63:02–63:03, becoming the new Women's Royal Rumble longevity record holder ahead of Ripley/Morgan's prior 1:01:08.

notableMoments.title: Valhalla ties the women's shortest-survival record after R-Truth disrupts her entrance
notableMoments.description: Valhalla tied the Women's Royal Rumble record for shortest survival time at 5 seconds (matching Chelsea Green's 2023 mark) after R-Truth disrupted her entrance, leading to her immediate elimination.

notableMoments.title: TNA's Jordynne Grace makes a cross-promotional surprise entrance at #5
notableMoments.description: Then-TNA Knockouts World Champion Jordynne Grace entered as a surprise at #5, an early cross-promotional appearance predating WWE-TNA's deeper formal partnership.

notableMoments.title: Liv Morgan returns after over six months out with injury
notableMoments.description: Liv Morgan competed in the 2024 Women's Rumble as part of her comeback after being out more than six months with injury.

notableMoments.title: Bayley becomes the first Mexican-American woman to win the Royal Rumble

notableMoments.title: Shotzi reportedly pulled at the last minute for returning Alexa Bliss
notableMoments.description: Shotzi Blackheart — who would have been making her 6th consecutive Women's Royal Rumble appearance (2020–2024) — was reportedly replaced at the last minute by Alexa Bliss, returning to action after roughly two years away. The report says there was "no heat between Shotzi and Bliss," but some in WWE "felt bad about how things ended up for Shotzi," even as "most were happy to see Alexa finally return to action."

notableMoments.title: Flair's return was shadowed by real anxiety after a torn ACL/MCL
notableMoments.description: Per WWE's Netflix docuseries "WWE Unreal," Charlotte Flair told Triple H after the match she wasn't sure how to react to the win; he told her to "always show emotions, just be real." Flair described 2024 as difficult after tearing her ACL and MCL, and said she'd been afraid of letting fans down on her return.

notableMoments.title: Liv Morgan wins after two prior runner-up finishes
notableMoments.description: Liv Morgan won her first Royal Rumble in 2026, on her third-consecutive appearance in the match's final two: she was runner-up to Rhea Ripley at RR2023W and to Bayley at RR2024W (confirmed directly by this database's own entrants records, is_runner_up=TRUE both years) before finally winning in 2026. The 2026 finish saw Morgan, Sol Ruca and Tiffany Stratton battling on the apron before Ruca went out in a ringpost collision and Morgan finished Stratton with an Ob-Liv-ion.

notableMoments.title: Charlotte Flair logs the longest survival time of the match — without winning

notableMoments.title: Reviewer critique: match felt "too rehearsed," no surprise AAA/TNA crossovers
notableMoments.description: Bleacher Report's Chris Mueller graded the women's match a relatively soft C+, criticizing it as feeling "a little too rehearsed" with choreographed-feeling sequences, and noted disappointment that no surprise entrants from AAA or TNA appeared despite pre-show speculation.

notableMoments.title: Michelle McCool led all eliminators with 5 credited eliminations; Nia Jax's literal total is 4, not 5
notableMoments.description: A literal walk-through of the official elimination table gives Michelle McCool the match's highest total credited-elimination count at 5 (4 solo -- Sonya Deville, Liv Morgan, Molly Holly, Lana -- plus a shared credit for Vickie Guerrero's group elimination). Nia Jax, tied for the most SOLO eliminations at 4 (Jacqueline, Kelly Kelly, Ruby Riott, Naomi), had zero group-elimination credits as an eliminator -- she was the victim, not a contributor, of the match's 6-way group elimination. Some secondary sources claim Nia Jax had 5 eliminations; this is contradicted by a literal, independently-verified walk-through of the official WWE.com/Wikipedia table and is treated as an error in those sources.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax eliminated in a 6-way group elimination
notableMoments.description: Nia Jax, who had herself eliminated 4 opponents, was eliminated in a single spot by six wrestlers acting together -- Asuka, Bayley, Brie Bella, Natalya, Nikki Bella and Trish Stratus -- after 17:56.

notableMoments.title: Nia Jax competed in both Royal Rumble matches the same night
notableMoments.description: Nia Jax entered #29 in this Women's Royal Rumble (eliminating Io Shirai and Natalya solo, plus a shared credit on Bayley, before being eliminated by Becky Lynch) and later the same night appeared as a surprise entrant in the Men's Royal Rumble as well -- becoming the first person to compete in (and score eliminations in) both Rumble matches on one card. See build_2019_men.py's NM066 for the fuller account, including a legitimate in-ring injury she caused there.

notableMoments.title: Eleven women eliminate Nia Jax
notableMoments.description: WWE's official RR2023W results explicitly state that the other 11 Superstars eliminated Nia Jax, and its Eliminated By table names Asuka, Lacey Evans, Liv Morgan, Michelle McCool, Michin, Nikki Cross, Piper Niven, Raquel Rodriguez, Rhea Ripley, Sonya Deville, and Shotzi. All 11 therefore receive structured assisted-elimination credit.

notableMoments.title: Kairi Sane replaced the injured Alicia Fox
notableMoments.description: Alicia Fox was originally scheduled to compete but suffered a broken tailbone shortly before the event and was pulled from both this match and the Mixed Match Challenge; Kairi Sane took her place, entering #6.

notableMoments.title: Alicia Fox briefly wins the 24/7 Championship
notableMoments.description: During the Royal Rumble, Alicia Fox pinned R-Truth to win the 24/7 Championship before Truth regained it moments later.

notableMoments.title: Alicia Fox broke her tailbone in rehearsal the day before, replaced last-minute by Kairi Sane
notableMoments.description: Alicia Fox, advertised for the inaugural Women's Royal Rumble, fractured her tailbone (coccyx) during a rehearsal walkthrough shortly before the event and had to be pulled from both the Rumble and the Mixed Match Challenge. NXT's Kairi Sane was brought in as a last-minute replacement, entering the historic match at #6; Fox was reported to be sidelined for several months.

notableMoments.title: Nine returning WWE alumnae brought back for the historic first edition
notableMoments.description: Lita, Jacqueline, Beth Phoenix, Trish Stratus, Michelle McCool, Torrie Wilson, Molly Holly, Kelly Kelly and Vickie Guerrero all returned for this inaugural match. Of these, only Lita, Jacqueline, Beth Phoenix and Trish Stratus were already WWE Hall of Famers at the time -- McCool, Torrie Wilson and Molly Holly were inducted years later (2025, 2019, 2021), and Kelly Kelly and Vickie Guerrero have never been inducted in their own right.

notableMoments.title: Beth Phoenix and Nia Jax's confrontation drew a "This is awesome" chant, and a "Divas of Doom" reunion was cut short
notableMoments.description: Beth Phoenix's Rumble return included a much-praised confrontation with Nia Jax that earned the Philadelphia crowd's "This is awesome!" chant. Phoenix briefly reunited with her old "Divas of Doom" tag partner Natalya during the match, but Natalya eliminated Phoenix shortly after.

notableMoments.title: Beth Phoenix busted open her head on the ring post
notableMoments.description: During a corner exchange with Bianca Belair, Phoenix threw her head back to sell a strike and struck the back of her head on the ring post, opening a cut. Dave Meltzer confirmed on air/in reporting that "Beth Phoenix hit the back of her head on the post so that's where all the blood was coming from." She continued wrestling while bleeding until being eliminated by Shayna Baszler near the end of the match.

notableMoments.title: Early Ripley/Brooke mistimed collision; McCool nearly falls off the barricade
notableMoments.description: Early in the women's Rumble, Rhea Ripley and Dana Brooke mistimed a spot and collided awkwardly. Later, Hall of Famer Michelle McCool, making a legends entrance from the crowd, nearly lost her balance and fell off the barricade.

notableMoments.title: Vince McMahon initially blocked Mickie James from wearing her Impact title on WWE TV
notableMoments.description: Vince McMahon reportedly forbade Mickie James from being shown wearing her Impact Wrestling Knockouts Championship on WWE programming the night of the Rumble. A producer informed him the title's appearance was contractually required, and McMahon reluctantly relented: "fuck it, fine!"

notableMoments.title: Shotzi reportedly pulled at the last minute for returning Alexa Bliss
notableMoments.description: Shotzi Blackheart — who would have been making her 6th consecutive Women's Royal Rumble appearance (2020–2024) — was reportedly replaced at the last minute by Alexa Bliss, returning to action after roughly two years away. The report says there was "no heat between Shotzi and Bliss," but some in WWE "felt bad about how things ended up for Shotzi," even as "most were happy to see Alexa finally return to action."

facts.title: Andre the Giant advertised, then quietly withdrawn over health concerns
facts.text: Andre the Giant was advertised for RR1991M for several weeks before his name was removed without public explanation, roughly 3 weeks before the event. WWE producer Bruce Prichard later explained it was purely health-driven: "It was health issues, it was the thought that we're not going to get Andre beyond this. Even bringing him out at number 30 wouldn't have been pretty."

facts.title: Brian Knobbs entered as a late substitute for The Honky Tonk Man
facts.text: The Honky Tonk Man, advertised for RR1991M, had quit the WWF weeks earlier (shortly after Christmas 1990). Brian Knobbs of The Nasty Boys took his place as a late substitution.

facts.title: Three expected entrants missed RR1992M for very different real-life reasons
facts.text: Brian Knobbs, Bret Hart, and Marty Jannetty were all expected for RR1992M but didn't appear, replaced in the field by Haku and Nikolai Volkoff. Knobbs was stabbed in a road-rage incident shortly before the event -- per softwolves.pp.se, stabbed 4 times by 3 fans on 1992-01-05 in Peoria, IL, while driving to a hotel with Jerry Sags and IRS after a card. Bret Hart's absence was written into the storyline as a 104-degree fever. Marty Jannetty's reason is a genuine source disagreement, preserved rather than picked: cultaholic frames it as being written out following the Shawn Michaels Superkick angle (the start of the real-life Rockers breakup storyline), while softwolves.pp.se instead says he "was actually fired" around this time.

facts.title: Rick Martel's 52:30 was the first Royal Rumble survival to pass 50 minutes
facts.text: Rick Martel's 52:30 survival time (this database's own CONFIRMED figure for his elimination by British Bulldog, S018;S019;S026) was, per cultaholic, the first time any wrestler had passed the 50-minute mark in Royal Rumble history. The record lasted exactly one year, broken by Ric Flair's 59:31 at RR1992M -- already documented in events.csv's RR1992M historical_significance field.

facts.title: Commentary allegedly re-recorded after the fact for Sid Justice's elimination of Hulk Hogan
facts.text: Per cultaholic, WWE re-recorded RR1992M's commentary track after the event to make Sid Justice's elimination of Hulk Hogan sound like a cheap shot rather than reflect the crowd's actual, reportedly more positive live reaction -- with Gorilla Monsoon dubbed calling Sid a "thief in the night" despite Sid's tactics being standard battle-royal play.

facts.title: Giant Gonzalez interrupted the match to attack The Undertaker -- without ever officially entering it
facts.text: Giant Gonzalez ran in partway through RR1993M and attacked The Undertaker, causing his elimination, despite never being an official Rumble entrant (this database's own source S027 explicitly excludes him from the active-wrestler ring-crowdedness count). Modeled in this database as a real eliminator credit -- a genuinely unusual case, distinct from every other year's 'illegally-assisted' eliminations, since those always involved a listed entrant. See flags.csv F053 for the full treatment.

facts.title: A Free-For-All pre-show match decided who got entry #1 and who got #30
facts.text: In the first-ever WWF pay-per-view Free-For-All pre-show, Duke Droese faced Hunter Hearst Helmsley with Rumble entry position on the line: the winner would get the final #30 spot, the loser would have to enter first at #1. Helmsley pinned Droese, but WWF president Gorilla Monsoon reversed the decision and disqualified Helmsley for using brass knuckles -- handing Droese the win and the coveted late entry. Matches this database's own already-CONFIRMED entry numbers exactly (Droese #30, Helmsley #1).

facts.title: Bret Hart eliminated Steve Austin unseen by the referees -- who then counted Austin's win anyway
facts.text: At 50:05, Bret Hart threw Steve Austin over the top rope, but the referees were distracted by a Mankind/Terry Funk brawl outside the ring and never saw it. Austin snuck back in undetected, eliminated The Undertaker and Vader, then eliminated Hart from behind to be declared the winner -- an outcome the match's own official record still reflects today. This database deliberately models the officiated (missed-call) result rather than the true sequence of events, treating it the same way the broadcast itself did. See flags.csv F081 for the full modeling rationale.

facts.title: Mil Mascaras eliminated himself with a dive he didn't need to make
facts.text: Mascaras threw his opponent outside the ring, then -- rather than simply staying in the match -- ducked through the middle rope, climbed to the turnbuckle from the ring apron, and dove onto his opponent outside, landing on his feet and eliminating himself in the process. The source narrative itself notes uncertainty about whether this even should have counted as 'going over the top' by the match's usual rule, but the referees ruled it a self-elimination on landing, citing Rick Martel's earlier Rumble as precedent. See flags.csv F082.

facts.title: Vince McMahon won the Royal Rumble -- then immediately gave away his own title shot
facts.text: With help from a distraction by The Rock, Vince McMahon eliminated Steve Austin last to win the match himself, denying Austin what would have been an unprecedented third straight Rumble win. McMahon is the only authority-figure/non-full-time-wrestler winner in this database's coverage so far. In a first for the Rumble, the winner then forfeited his own WrestleMania title-match reward; Commissioner Shawn Michaels awarded it instead to runner-up Austin, 'much to McMahon's fury,' setting up Austin's WrestleMania XV title win.

facts.title: The Rock's feet hit the floor before Big Show's on the winning elimination -- but Rock was declared the winner anyway
facts.text: In the match's final exchange, The Rock eliminated Big Show using Show's own momentum, but in doing so The Rock's own feet touched the floor outside the ring a beat before Big Show's did -- by the match's own rules, arguably Big Show, not Rock, should have won. Referees declared The Rock the winner regardless. Big Show spent the following weeks claiming he had 'indisputable video evidence' of the real result; Triple H reviewed it on-air but the decision stood. Years later, The Rock himself publicly agreed Big Show 'legitimately should have been declared the winner.'

facts.title: Drew Carey's celebrity cameo entry -- and quick self-elimination
facts.text: Entering at #5, comedian Drew Carey's appearance came from an on-screen storyline: Vince McMahon pulled a promised pre-show Sunday Night Heat winner's slot and gave it to Carey instead, reportedly hoping he'd be pummeled. Carey safely climbed over the top rope to self-eliminate almost immediately -- one of the more purely comedic moments in Rumble history, and per this database's own sourcing, a factor in his later WWE Hall of Fame celebrity-wing induction.

facts.title: Steve Austin drew #27 -- but was physically the last man to enter the ring
facts.text: Austin was attacked in the aisle by Triple H (payback for costing HHH his title match earlier that night) before he could physically enter. Per this database's timing analysis his actual ring-entry moment lands 1 second after the officially-numbered #30 entrant (Rikishi) -- Austin fought his way in by throwing an already-attacked Rikishi into the ring ahead of him. entry_number is kept at his drawn/announced 27 (this database's standard convention); see flags.csv F130 for the full multi-source resolution of this event's exact mechanics.

facts.title: Maven's dropkick elimination of The Undertaker -- one of the Rumble's most famous upsets
facts.text: A total underdog at the time, Maven caught The Undertaker on the ring apron with a dropkick and eliminated one of the promotion's most dominant stars -- widely regarded as one of the most famous surprise eliminations in Royal Rumble history. Undertaker then brutally beat Maven down outside the ring; no reliable source specifies who formally eliminated Maven afterward, so that follow-up elimination is left UNKNOWN rather than guessed (see F163).

facts.title: Mr. Perfect's surprise one-off return, six years after leaving the WWF
facts.text: Curt Hennig made a surprise return to the WWF after a 6-year absence, reaching the Final Four before Triple H eliminated him. Per this database's own S049 sourcing, this was 'the last notable thing Hennig would do' before his death in February 2003, just over a year later.

facts.title: Batista's chair-shot return after his own elimination
facts.text: After being legitimately eliminated by The Undertaker in the Final Four, Batista came back in with a steel chair as pure interference before Undertaker tossed him out a second time. Not modeled as a second entrant row or elimination in this database -- Batista's official (first and only legitimate) entry and elimination is what's recorded, the same principle used for 1997's Giant Gonzalez interference (F081/NM006) and 2000/2002's similar cases.

facts.title: Test was advertised for #21 -- but Mick Foley, his storyline attacker, showed up instead
facts.text: Test was advertised for entry #21 but was shown 'lying beat up in the back' after a storyline attack; Mick Foley, revealed as the attacker, entered in his place to the crowd's delight. Modeled with two entrant rows sharing entry_number 21 -- Test (no elimination logged, the same no-show convention used for Randy Savage 1991, Bastion Booger 1994 and Skull 1998) and Foley, the wrestler who actually competed at that slot.

facts.title: The Foley/Orton double-clothesline spot -- a shared elimination that spilled onto the floor
facts.text: Foley and Randy Orton went over the top rope together in a single simultaneous clothesline spot, with the brawl continuing on the floor outside. Modeled as two elimination rows sharing simultaneous_group_id 'foley_orton_double_clothesline': Orton eliminated by Foley, and Foley self-eliminated -- the same self-elimination convention used for Drew Carey (2001, see NM012) and Kane's self-elimination in 1999.

facts.title: Vince McMahon tore both quads for real sorting out the botched Batista/Cena finish
facts.text: Batista and Cena appeared to go over the top rope simultaneously in a botched spot. Officials, including a diving Vince McMahon, spent 2 minutes 35 seconds (excluded from the match's official running time) sorting out the confusion -- McMahon suffered a genuine torn quadriceps in both legs in the process, before the match was restarted and Batista hit a spinebuster to officially eliminate Cena for the win. Per a former WWE referee/producer and Cena's own later on-record podcast account ('I know I f*cked up... that was me'), Batista winning was always the planned finish -- the botch was a pure execution error, not a change of plan.

facts.title: Kurt Angle, already eliminated, dragged Shawn Michaels into the Ankle Lock
facts.text: Angle was eliminated by a Shawn Michaels superkick, then ran back into the match afterward -- no longer a legal competitor -- and dragged Michaels from the ring into the Ankle Lock. The source material explicitly narrates Angle, not an unnamed party, as physically performing Michaels's elimination, so this database credits Angle as HBK's official eliminator despite not being an active competitor at the time -- a deliberate exception to the usual officiated-record convention (see F184). This attack launched one of 2005's best feuds.

facts.title: Kane's then-record 8th consecutive Royal Rumble appearance -- PROBABLE, not CONFIRMED
facts.text: Per a single independent stats-blog source (Rumblemetrics), Kane's 2006 entry marked his then-record 8th consecutive Royal Rumble appearance. Not independently cross-checked against a second source this pass, so logged here at PROBABLE rather than CONFIRMED -- a deliberate example of this database surfacing an interesting single-sourced claim honestly rather than silently upgrading its confidence.

facts.title: The Undertaker/Shawn Michaels final segment -- "one of the best finishes to any Rumble ever"
facts.text: The Undertaker's first career Royal Rumble win was capped by an approximately 8-minute final one-on-one stretch against Shawn Michaels, met with a standing ovation and widely praised afterward -- TJR Wrestling calls it 'the best finish to any Rumble ever,' language this database's own sourcing independently echoes ('one of the best finishing sequences to a Royal Rumble ever'). Set up Undertaker's WrestleMania 23 World Heavyweight Championship win over Batista.

facts.title: The first Royal Rumble with entrants from all 3 WWE brands
facts.text: RR2007M was the first Royal Rumble to feature entrants from Raw, SmackDown AND ECW since ECW became a full third WWE brand following its 2006 revival -- confirmed by TJR Wrestling's retrospective coverage.

facts.title: John Cena's shock return from injury as the surprise #30 entrant -- and he won
facts.text: Cena had been out for roughly 3 months with a torn pectoral muscle and was not advertised for the match. He returned as the surprise final (#30) entrant to a huge reaction and went on to win his first Royal Rumble.

facts.title: Hornswoggle spent nearly 26 minutes hiding under the ring before being forced into the match
facts.text: Hornswoggle's participation this year is one of this database's more unusual timing cases: he spent 25 minutes 45 seconds hiding under the ring before being forced in, then voluntarily left the ring and returned backstage without ever going over the top rope -- modeled as a self-elimination, the same convention used for Kane (1999) and Drew Carey (2001). His storyline partner Finlay was disqualified during the same sequence, a rare disqualification in Royal Rumble history.

facts.title: Santino Marella's 0:02 survival time -- the shortest in Royal Rumble history
facts.text: Santino Marella was eliminated just 2 seconds after entering, setting a new record for shortest survival time in Royal Rumble history and breaking The Warlord's mark from 1989.

facts.title: Edge's 7:19 ring time -- the shortest ever by a Royal Rumble winner
facts.text: Edge entered as a surprise #29 entrant, returning from a torn Achilles tendon suffered mid-2009, and won after just 7 minutes 19 seconds in the match -- a record for shortest time spent in the match by an eventual winner, which stood until Brock Lesnar broke it in 2022.

facts.title: Beth Phoenix becomes only the second woman ever to compete in a standard 30-man Royal Rumble
facts.text: Beth Phoenix became just the second woman to compete in a standard 30-man Royal Rumble match, after Chyna (1999 and 2000). She eliminated The Great Khali by distracting him with a kiss before being eliminated herself by CM Punk.

facts.title: The first-ever 40-man Royal Rumble match
facts.text: RR2011M was the first-ever 40-man Royal Rumble match -- every prior year from 1988-2010 had used the standard 30-man field. Billed going in as 'the biggest Royal Rumble match in history.'

facts.title: The entire WWE commentary team entered the match as competitors
facts.text: RR2012M notably featured the entire WWE commentary team -- Michael Cole, Jerry Lawler, and Booker T -- entering the match as competitors, a gimmick not repeated in most other years.

facts.title: Kofi Kingston's walking-handstand escape
facts.text: Kofi Kingston pulled off a widely remembered walking-handstand escape to save himself from elimination, going on to survive an additional 7 minutes 45 seconds afterward.

facts.title: The Miz's non-entrant interference elimination of John Cena
facts.text: John Cena's eliminator, The Miz, was not an entrant in this Royal Rumble match at all -- Miz ran in from outside, with Alex Riley's distraction, while defending the WWE Championship elsewhere on the same card. An unusual non-participant interference elimination, agreed on by 2 independent sources.

facts.title: Big Show eliminated two pairs of wrestlers before his own official entry
facts.text: Big Show's eliminations of Jack Swagger, and of the Miz and Cody Rhodes together, both occurred before his own entry_actual time (46:32) -- during his roughly 1:47 entrance walk, interfering from ringside before formally entering the ring. Directly narrated by a single source (S084, Shane's own frame-by-frame timing analysis) and modeled as-is; not independently cross-checked this pass, so logged here at PROBABLE rather than CONFIRMED.

facts.title: John Cena's 2nd Rumble win -- one of only two ever from a #9-21 entry draw
facts.text: Cena won his 2nd Royal Rumble (after 2008), entering at #19. Per WrestlingInc's stats roundup, he is one of only two wrestlers ever to win a 30-man Royal Rumble having drawn an entry number between #9 and #21 -- the other being Shawn Michaels in 1996.

facts.title: The Godfather's farewell Royal Rumble, 20 years and 5 gimmicks after his debut
facts.text: The Godfather made his final Royal Rumble appearance this year, 20 years after his first Rumble appearance (1993, as Papa Shango) -- per the SE Scoops stats roundup, he competed under 5 different ring gimmicks across his Rumble history.

facts.title: Roman Reigns's broadcast-record 12 eliminations sparked a fan backlash when Batista won
facts.text: Reigns, in his Rumble debut, was broadcast-credited with a Rumble-record 12 eliminations and was the clear live-crowd favorite, while Batista -- a part-time returning veteran -- was booed heavily for winning instead, in a moment that sparked a well-known, lasting fan backlash. This database's own guest-analyst source recalculates Reigns's total at 9.5 under an even-split partial-credit system for shared eliminations (see F277); that recalculation remains single-sourced and has not been corroborated by any other source checked, so it is noted here honestly rather than adopted as a second confirmed figure.

facts.title: Rey Mysterio was the surprise "Not Daniel Bryan" #30 entrant
facts.text: The 30th and final entrant was Rey Mysterio -- a slot Shane's own source document labels 'Not Daniel Bryan,' after the surprise Bryan entrance fans had widely been expecting instead. Mysterio's identity as the deflating surprise entrant is independently confirmed via multiple post-event sources, including Daniel Bryan's and Mysterio's own public comments.

facts.title: Xavier Woods was reportedly an official entrant who never got a spot in the match
facts.text: Xavier Woods was reportedly announced/drawn as an official entrant for this match but never actually appeared in it. Single-sourced this pass (Shane's guest-analyst source, cross-checked against Woods's own match-history record for plausibility) -- logged as PROBABLE rather than CONFIRMED.

facts.title: Daniel Bryan's early elimination sparked heavy boos for Roman Reigns's win in Philadelphia
facts.text: Reigns's win, entering at #19 and eliminating Rusev in the match's final moments, was met with heavy boos from the live Philadelphia crowd, still upset over Daniel Bryan's comparatively early elimination (10:11 survival, only the 10th-longest of the match). A surprise late appearance from The Rock, endorsing Reigns and physically confronting the already-eliminated Big Show and Kane, did not turn the crowd.

facts.title: Curtis Axel was counted as an entrant with a 0:00 survival time after being substituted before he could enter
facts.text: Curtis Axel was counted as an official entrant with a 0:00 survival time after being attacked and substituted for by Erick Rowan before he could ever enter the ring -- Rowan himself is explicitly excluded as an official competitor by the source material. This participation-status modeling is strongly corroborated by 5 independent sources.

facts.title: At 61:43, the longest Royal Rumble match timed in this database at the time
facts.text: This match ran an unusually long 61 minutes 43 seconds -- the longest Royal Rumble match timed in this document's entire multi-year data set at the time of writing.

facts.title: The WWE Championship was defended -- and lost -- inside the Rumble match itself
facts.text: Roman Reigns, the reigning WWE Champion, entered at #1 and defended the title WITHIN the match itself, only the second time in Royal Rumble history a world title was decided by the match itself (after Ric Flair in 1992). He lost the title when Triple H won the match, becoming WWE Champion by winning the Rumble.

facts.title: Brock Lesnar was eliminated in a group interference spot by "the entire Wyatt Family"
facts.text: Brock Lesnar was eliminated in a group interference spot originally credited only to 'the entire Wyatt Family.' Individually named via 3 independent sources -- WWE.com's own official recap, a Wrestling Inc retro review, and allrumblestats.com's data table -- which agree the participants were Braun Strowman (in his Rumble debut, going on to eliminate both Kane and Big Show back-to-back later in the match), Erick Rowan, and Luke Harper.

facts.title: Randy Orton's 2nd Royal Rumble win -- the 7th multi-time winner in history
facts.text: Orton won his 2nd Royal Rumble (after 2009), becoming the 7th wrestler to win the Royal Rumble more than once, joining Hulk Hogan, Steve Austin, Shawn Michaels, Triple H, John Cena and Batista.

facts.title: Tye Dillinger's "Perfect 10" entrance at #10
facts.text: Dillinger's NXT call-up drew entry #10 -- a perfect match for his 'Perfect 10' gimmick -- producing one of the most-remembered reactions of the match, even though he was eliminated 8th, after 5:27.

facts.title: Roman Reigns wrestled twice in one night -- losing the Universal Championship, then nearly winning the Rumble
facts.text: Reigns lost the WWE Universal Championship to Kevin Owens in a No Disqualification match earlier the same card (with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage above the ring), then entered the Royal Rumble at #30, eliminated The Undertaker, and made the final two before losing to Randy Orton.

facts.title: James Ellsworth's 15-second Rumble run, among the shortest ever
facts.text: Ellsworth entered #11 as part of a comedy angle and was eliminated by Braun Strowman in just 0:15 -- one of the shortest Royal Rumble appearances on record.

facts.title: Braun Strowman's 7 eliminations, the most of the match
facts.text: Strowman eliminated 7 competitors (Big Cass, Kalisto, Mojo Rawley, Mark Henry, Big Show, James Ellsworth, Tye Dillinger) -- the most of this match, though not yet the all-time single-Rumble record, which stood at 11 (Kane, RR2001) at the time. Strowman broke that record the following year, at the 2018 Greatest Royal Rumble in Saudi Arabia -- outside this database's current scope.

facts.title: Goldberg eliminated Brock Lesnar, previewing their WrestleMania 33 title feud
facts.text: Goldberg, an unaffiliated returning legend entering at #28, eliminated Brock Lesnar -- the beginning of a rivalry that culminated in Goldberg winning the Universal Championship from Lesnar at WrestleMania 33 in a match lasting under two minutes.

facts.title: The last men's-only Royal Rumble before the Women's Royal Rumble debuted in 2018
facts.text: This was the final Royal Rumble PPV to feature only a men's Rumble match -- the first Women's Royal Rumble match was introduced the following year, at Royal Rumble 2018.

facts.title: Shinsuke Nakamura wins the Royal Rumble in his first attempt
facts.text: Nakamura entered #14 and won by eliminating Roman Reigns, choosing to challenge AJ Styles for the WWE Championship at WrestleMania 34.

facts.title: The New Day's 'pancake save' for Kofi Kingston
facts.text: Xavier Woods and Big E cushioned a near-elimination for Kingston at ringside with a platform of pancakes, a widely-replayed comedic spot -- Kingston was eliminated by Andrade a short time later anyway.

facts.title: Matt Hardy and Bray Wyatt eliminated each other simultaneously
facts.text: Wikipedia's table carries an explicit footnote noting Hardy and Wyatt eliminated each other at the same moment -- notable in hindsight since the two became the 'Deleters of Worlds' tag team later in 2018.

facts.title: Rey Mysterio's surprise return after leaving WWE in 2015
facts.text: Mysterio entered at #27, his first WWE appearance in roughly 3 years -- at the time he was working AAA/Lucha Underground, with contemporary reporting uncertain whether this was a one-off nostalgia spot. He eliminated Adam Cole before being eliminated himself by Finn Balor, lasting 9:40.

facts.title: Finn Balor's 57:38 was the longest individual time of the match
facts.text: Balor entered #2 and survived 57:38 -- fully agreed across all sources as the match's 'Iron Man' -- while also eliminating 4 opponents (Baron Corbin, Aiden English, Rey Mysterio, Dolph Ziggler), tied for the match high.

facts.title: The Bar won the Raw Tag Team Championship earlier the same card, then Cesaro and Sheamus entered the Rumble as reigning champions
facts.text: Cesaro and Sheamus (as The Bar) defeated Seth Rollins & Jason Jordan for the Raw Tag Team Championship earlier on this card. Rollins, having just lost the title, also entered the Rumble later that night at #18; Cesaro and Sheamus entered at #15 and #11 respectively as the reigning champions.

facts.title: Asuka wins the first-ever Women's Royal Rumble match
facts.text: Asuka entered #25 and won by eliminating Nikki Bella, becoming the first winner in the history of the Women's Royal Rumble match -- the second women's match ever to main event a WWE pay-per-view, and the first to main event one of WWE's 'Big Four' shows (direct Wikipedia characterization).

facts.title: Ronda Rousey's surprise debut overshadowed Asuka's win, per contemporary criticism
facts.text: Immediately after Asuka's win, Ronda Rousey's music hit and she came to the ring to confirm her full-time WWE signing -- cutting into what should have been Asuka's championship-opponent-selection moment; Asuka reportedly declined to shake Rousey's hand. Sports Illustrated's Justin Barrasso wrote the next day: "the show should have finished by celebrating the winner of the women's Rumble. Instead, we were treated to the Ronda Rousey show," adding the finish "ended with her as an afterthought." A second outlet, FanSided, made a similar argument the same day. This is a genuine, contemporary (within-24-hours) point of criticism from 2 independent sources.

facts.title: Reigning champions Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair were not entrants
facts.text: The reigning Raw and SmackDown Women's Champions, Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair, did not compete in this Rumble despite holding the two women's titles at the time -- both came to the ring only after the match concluded to confront Asuka about her upcoming title choice.

facts.title: Kairi Sane replaced the injured Alicia Fox
facts.text: Alicia Fox was originally scheduled to compete but suffered a broken tailbone shortly before the event and was pulled from both this match and the Mixed Match Challenge; Kairi Sane took her place, entering #6.

facts.title: Michelle McCool led all eliminators with 5 credited eliminations; Nia Jax's literal total is 4, not 5
facts.text: A literal walk-through of the official elimination table gives Michelle McCool the match's highest total credited-elimination count at 5 (4 solo -- Sonya Deville, Liv Morgan, Molly Holly, Lana -- plus a shared credit for Vickie Guerrero's group elimination). Nia Jax, tied for the most SOLO eliminations at 4 (Jacqueline, Kelly Kelly, Ruby Riott, Naomi), had zero group-elimination credits as an eliminator -- she was the victim, not a contributor, of the match's 6-way group elimination. Some secondary sources claim Nia Jax had 5 eliminations; this is contradicted by a literal, independently-verified walk-through of the official WWE.com/Wikipedia table and is treated as an error in those sources.

facts.title: Nia Jax eliminated in a 6-way group elimination
facts.text: Nia Jax, who had herself eliminated 4 opponents, was eliminated in a single spot by six wrestlers acting together -- Asuka, Bayley, Brie Bella, Natalya, Nikki Bella and Trish Stratus -- after 17:56.

facts.title: Sasha Banks eliminated by the Bella Twins after the match's longest individual survival time
facts.text: Sasha Banks, the opening (#1) entrant, survived 54:46 -- the longest individual time of the match -- before being eliminated in a shared spot by Nikki Bella and Brie Bella.

facts.title: Nine returning WWE alumnae brought back for the historic first edition
facts.text: Lita, Jacqueline, Beth Phoenix, Trish Stratus, Michelle McCool, Torrie Wilson, Molly Holly, Kelly Kelly and Vickie Guerrero all returned for this inaugural match. Of these, only Lita, Jacqueline, Beth Phoenix and Trish Stratus were already WWE Hall of Famers at the time -- McCool, Torrie Wilson and Molly Holly were inducted years later (2025, 2019, 2021), and Kelly Kelly and Vickie Guerrero have never been inducted in their own right.

facts.title: Seth Rollins wins the Royal Rumble in his first attempt
facts.text: Rollins entered #10 and won by eliminating Braun Strowman, surviving 43:00 (the match's longest individual time), earning a Universal Championship match against Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 35 -- which he won, becoming Universal Champion.

facts.title: Nia Jax becomes the first person to compete in both Royal Rumble matches on the same night
facts.text: Nia Jax, a Women's-division wrestler, attacked advertised #30 entrant R-Truth on the ramp before he could enter and took his spot in the Men's Royal Rumble -- becoming the first person to compete in both the men's and women's Rumble matches on the same card, and the first to score an elimination in both (eliminating Mustafa Ali here; see build_2019_women.py for her women's-match appearance). Per Jerry Lawler's own podcast account, the scripted attack legitimately hurt R-Truth (ankle and face).

facts.title: The Mustafa Ali/Nia Jax elimination spot was originally meant for someone else
facts.text: Per Mustafa Ali's own later interview, the spot in which Nia Jax eliminated him was originally designed for a different, unnamed wrestler who declined it, uncomfortable being eliminated by a woman. Ali volunteered as the replacement, reportedly at Jamie Noble's request. This is a separate matter from Nia Jax's legitimate injuring of R-Truth earlier in the same match (see NM066) -- Ali later suffered an unrelated concussion at a house show in February 2019, not connected to the Rumble.

facts.title: Braun Strowman led all eliminators, with a disputed exact total
facts.text: Braun Strowman was widely reported as having the most eliminations of the match. A literal box-score walk of the table gives him 6 (4 solo -- Shelton Benjamin, Baron Corbin, Andrade, Dolph Ziggler -- plus shared credits on Jeff Hardy and Drew McIntyre); Fightful.com's own published stats article instead states 5, likely not crediting him on the McIntyre spot. See flags.csv F381.

facts.title: Shinsuke Nakamura won the United States Championship hours before entering the Rumble
facts.text: Nakamura defeated Rusev to win the United States Championship on the Kickoff Show, then entered the Men's Royal Rumble at #3 as reigning champion -- the only confirmed Rumble entrant who also wrestled earlier on the same card.

facts.title: Two reigning NXT/NXT UK champions entered as surprise call-ups
facts.text: Johnny Gargano entered #6 as reigning NXT North American Champion (won from Ricochet the night before at NXT TakeOver: Phoenix); Pete Dunne entered #18 as reigning NXT UK Champion (a reign stretching back to May 2017). Neither title was on the line in this non-title match.

facts.title: Ziggler/McIntyre Rumble spot paid off their late-2018 tag team split
facts.text: Drew McIntyre and Dolph Ziggler had been a Raw Tag Team Championship-winning duo (won Sept 3, 2018) who lost the titles Oct 22, 2018 and split in December 2018 after a steel cage match. Ziggler eliminated McIntyre from this Rumble by launching him over Braun Strowman's back, a storyline payoff of that feud -- neither man held a title at the time.

facts.title: Becky Lynch wins the Royal Rumble hours after losing her own title match
facts.text: Lynch lost her SmackDown Women's Championship match to Asuka earlier the same card, then was allowed to take injured advertised entrant Lana's vacated #28 slot -- entering, in practice, after #30 Carmella had already gone in. She eliminated Nia Jax and then Charlotte Flair for the winning elimination after surviving 13:20, earning a spot in the WrestleMania 35 winner-take-all triple threat (also featuring Ronda Rousey and Charlotte Flair), which she won -- becoming the first woman to hold both women's titles simultaneously and headlining the first-ever women's WrestleMania main event.

facts.title: Lana's storyline injury opened the door for Becky Lynch
facts.text: Lana was drawn/assigned the #28 slot and came out as that entrant, but a storyline ankle injury -- suffered when Rusev accidentally knocked her off the ring apron during his Kickoff Show US Championship match -- kept her from actually competing. She has no wrestler_id/entrant row in this database, matching this database's precedent for scheduled-but-never-entered wrestlers.

facts.title: Nia Jax competed in both Royal Rumble matches the same night
facts.text: Nia Jax entered #29 in this Women's Royal Rumble (eliminating Io Shirai and Natalya solo, plus a shared credit on Bayley, before being eliminated by Becky Lynch) and later the same night appeared as a surprise entrant in the Men's Royal Rumble as well -- becoming the first person to compete in (and score eliminations in) both Rumble matches on one card. See build_2019_men.py's NM066 for the fuller account, including a legitimate in-ring injury she caused there.

facts.title: Mandy Rose eliminated Naomi despite already being eliminated herself
facts.text: A direct Wikipedia footnote confirms Mandy Rose, having already been eliminated moments earlier, reached back into the ring from the floor and pulled Naomi out -- an unusual blown-spot moment that nonetheless stood as her official elimination credit.

facts.title: Natalya's 56:01 was the longest individual women's Royal Rumble survival time to date
facts.text: Natalya entered #2 and survived 56:01, the longest individual time in Women's Royal Rumble history at the time -- a record that stood until Bianca Belair broke it in 2021.

facts.title: Charlotte Flair led all eliminators with 5 credited eliminations
facts.text: Charlotte Flair (entered #13, runner-up) eliminated Xia Li, Tamina, Lacey Evans and Carmella solo, plus a shared credit on Bayley's elimination -- the match's highest total, before being eliminated herself by Becky Lynch for the winning elimination.

facts.title: Brock Lesnar ties the all-time single-Rumble elimination record with 13
facts.text: Entering at #1, Brock Lesnar eliminated 13 opponents in a row (11 solo, plus Keith Lee and Braun Strowman -- see F396) before being eliminated himself by Drew McIntyre after surviving 26:24 -- tying the all-time record for most eliminations by a single competitor in one Royal Rumble match.

facts.title: Drew McIntyre wins his first Royal Rumble
facts.text: McIntyre entered #16 and won by eliminating Roman Reigns with a Claymore Kick, surviving 34:11 (the match's longest individual time). He earned a WWE Championship match of his choosing at WrestleMania 36, which he used to challenge and defeat Brock Lesnar -- the same wrestler he had just eliminated from this Rumble.

facts.title: Edge's surprise in-ring return
facts.text: Edge, retired since 2011 due to a career-threatening neck injury and a WWE Hall of Famer, made a surprise in-ring comeback entering #21, surviving 23:43 (the match's 2nd-longest individual time) and eliminating AJ Styles, Luke Gallows and Randy Orton before being eliminated by Roman Reigns. Widely described as the show's marquee angle.

facts.title: Seth Rollins's 'Monday Night Messiah' alliance picks off a brief Owens/Black/Joe trio
facts.text: Kevin Owens, Aleister Black, and Samoa Joe briefly formed their own in-ring alliance before being picked off consecutively by Seth Rollins, who was backed throughout the match by outside interference from Akam and Rezar (Authors of Pain) as part of his heel-authority 'Monday Night Messiah' storyline. Owens, Black, Joe and Rollins's associates brawled to the back together after Rollins's own elimination.

facts.title: Four different championships were represented in the field
facts.text: This match featured 5 reigning champions across 4 titles: Brock Lesnar (WWE Championship), Kofi Kingston & Big E (SmackDown Tag Team Championship, as a duo), Shinsuke Nakamura (Intercontinental Championship), and Keith Lee (NXT North American Championship, won just 4 days earlier). None of these titles were defended within the match itself.

facts.title: Shayna Baszler and Bianca Belair tie for the most eliminations in Women's Royal Rumble history
facts.text: Both Shayna Baszler (entrant #30, runner-up) and Bianca Belair (entrant #2) recorded 8 credited eliminations apiece, tying for the most eliminations by a single competitor in Women's Royal Rumble history and breaking the prior record of 7, held by Nia Jax (RR2018W).

facts.title: Charlotte Flair wins her first Royal Rumble
facts.text: Charlotte Flair entered #17 and won by eliminating Shayna Baszler after surviving 27:19, becoming the first Royal Rumble winner in this database's separate RR2020W record. Her post-match promo was described by contemporary recaps as tonally ambiguous, neither clearly face nor heel.

facts.title: Santino Marella returns as 'Santina' for a comedic self-elimination
facts.text: Santino Marella returned in his 'Santina' drag persona at #29 and eliminated himself using his own 'Cobra' sock-puppet finishing move on himself -- confirmed by 2+ independent sources.

facts.title: Kairi Sane entered as a reigning champion, correcting an initial working assumption
facts.text: Kairi Sane entered #11 as reigning WWE Women's Tag Team Champion alongside Asuka (The Kabuki Warriors, won Oct 6, 2019) -- not Alexa Bliss and Nikki Cross, who did not win the titles until WrestleMania 36 months later, an assumption corrected during this build's research. See F404.

facts.title: Otis 'saves' Mandy Rose in a storyline interference spot
facts.text: Earlier in the match, Mandy Rose was saved from apparent elimination by Otis in a storyline spot connected to the Fire & Desire/Heavy Machinery angle -- praised across multiple contemporary recaps as a standout moment.

facts.title: Edge wins from the No. 1 entry
facts.text: Edge entered at No. 1 and won the 2021 Men's Royal Rumble, lasting WWE's official 58:27 and last eliminating Randy Orton.

facts.title: The first two entrants become the final two
facts.text: Edge and Randy Orton entered first and second and ultimately became the final two, after Orton spent much of the match outside the ring following the opening injury angle without being eliminated.

facts.title: Christian returns for his first true match since 2014
facts.text: Christian entered at No. 24 in a surprise return, reunited with Edge in the ring, reached the final four and lasted WWE's official 18:12.

facts.title: Non-entrant Omos eliminates Big E and Rey Mysterio
facts.text: Omos, who was at ringside with AJ Styles but was not an official entrant, was officially credited by WWE with eliminating Big E and Rey Mysterio.

facts.title: Bianca Belair wins from No. 3
facts.text: Bianca Belair entered at No. 3 and won, with WWE listing 56:52 of survival time.

facts.title: Rhea Ripley records seven eliminations
facts.text: WWE credits Rhea Ripley with a match-high seven eliminations.

facts.title: Alicia Fox briefly wins the 24/7 Championship
facts.text: During the Royal Rumble, Alicia Fox pinned R-Truth to win the 24/7 Championship before Truth regained it moments later.

facts.title: Official Carmella eliminator credit differs by source
facts.text: WWE lists Tamina as Carmella’s eliminator before Tamina entered the match, while Cagematch lists Reginald; the structured elimination follows WWE’s higher-tier official result.

facts.title: Brock Lesnar wins from No. 30
facts.text: Lesnar entered at No. 30 and won after five eliminations.

facts.title: Bad Bunny returns
facts.text: Bad Bunny returned as a surprise celebrity entrant and recorded two eliminations.

facts.title: Johnny Knoxville enters
facts.text: Johnny Knoxville entered at No. 9 and was eliminated by Sami Zayn.

facts.title: Omos group elimination
facts.text: Six official entrants combined to eliminate Omos.

facts.title: Ronda Rousey returns and wins
facts.text: Rousey returned at No. 28 and won.

facts.title: Mickie James enters as Impact champion
facts.text: WWE acknowledged Mickie James as reigning Impact Knockouts World Champion.

facts.title: Sonya Deville eliminates Naomi after elimination
facts.text: Deville returned after her own elimination and WWE officially credited her with eliminating Naomi.

facts.title: Mighty Molly surprise return
facts.text: Molly Holly entered under her Mighty Molly presentation.

facts.title: Cody Rhodes wins from No. 30
facts.text: Rhodes returned from injury at No. 30 and won by last eliminating Gunther.

facts.title: Gunther lasts 71:40
facts.text: Gunther entered No. 1 and survived 1:11:40, reaching the final two.

facts.title: Rey Mysterio does not appear
facts.text: Mysterio was assigned No. 17 but never appeared or entered the ring.

facts.title: Ricochet and Logan Paul collide
facts.text: Ricochet and Logan Paul launched from opposite sides and collided in mid-air.

facts.title: Rhea Ripley wins from No. 1
facts.text: Ripley became the first woman to win the Royal Rumble from the No. 1 position.

facts.title: Ripley and Morgan go wire-to-wire
facts.text: The No. 1 and No. 2 entrants became the final two after each lasting more than 61 minutes.

facts.title: Chelsea Green eliminated in five seconds
facts.text: Returning Chelsea Green was eliminated by Ripley after five seconds.

facts.title: Eleven women eliminate Nia Jax
facts.text: WWE's official RR2023W results explicitly state that the other 11 Superstars eliminated Nia Jax, and its Eliminated By table names Asuka, Lacey Evans, Liv Morgan, Michelle McCool, Michin, Nikki Cross, Piper Niven, Raquel Rodriguez, Rhea Ripley, Sonya Deville, and Shotzi. All 11 therefore receive structured assisted-elimination credit.

facts.title: Cody Rhodes wins consecutive Rumbles
facts.text: Rhodes followed his 2023 victory by last eliminating CM Punk.

facts.title: The Usos open against each other
facts.text: The brothers started at entries one and two after their split.

facts.title: Pat McAfee enters, then eliminates himself
facts.text: McAfee left commentary for entry 22, entered the ring and jumped out.

facts.title: CM Punk suffers a triceps injury
facts.text: Punk reached the final two; on the following Raw he disclosed a triceps injury sustained in the Rumble.

facts.title: Bayley sets women's survival record
facts.text: Naomi exceeded the previous mark before Bayley finished with the official 63:03 record.

facts.title: Jade Cargill's first WWE match
facts.text: Cargill entered at 28 and eliminated Jax.

facts.title: R-Truth mistakes the women's Rumble for his match
facts.text: Truth's interruption preceded Valhalla's entry; he was not an official competitor.

facts.title: Valhalla lasts five seconds
facts.text: Her official five-second duration matched Chelsea Green's 2023 low.

facts.title: TNA champion crosses into WWE
facts.text: Grace entered while holding the TNA Knockouts World Championship.

facts.title: IShowSpeed replaces attacked Akira Tozawa
facts.text: Both assigned and actual entrant retained at slot8.

facts.title: Jey Uso wins his first Royal Rumble
facts.text: Uso last eliminated Cena to earn a WrestleMania title match.

facts.title: Longest Royal Rumble match to date
facts.text: Independent timing80:10 exceeds the2018 Greatest Royal Rumble; duration disagreement flagged.

facts.title: Penta early floor-contact dispute
facts.text: Independent analysis questions an early apparent two-foot contact; no official elimination was ruled, so retain later Finn Balor elimination.

facts.title: Rollins attacks Reigns after elimination
facts.text: Punk eliminated Rollins and Reigns; Rollins attacked Reigns afterward.

facts.title: Charlotte becomes first two-time womens Rumble winner
facts.text: Flair followed2020 victory by last eliminating Perez.

facts.title: Roxanne sets womens survival record
facts.text: Official and independent timing agree at1:07:47.

facts.title: Nia Jax earns nine eliminations
facts.text: WWE names nine victims including pre-entry Zelina elimination and five-woman sweep; all credited individually.

facts.title: Alexa Bliss returns after two-year absence
facts.text: Bliss returned at entry21; Charlotte and Hall of Famers Stratus/Bella also returned.

facts.title: Royce Keys makes WWE debut
facts.text: Former Powerhouse Hobbs entered at14 under his new ring name.

facts.title: Both El Grande Americanos collide
facts.text: Returning original masked wrestler eliminated the second incarnation.

facts.title: Masked attack precedes Breakker elimination
facts.text: An unidentified masked attacker assaulted Breakker before he entered; Femi then eliminated him first. No attacker identity guessed.

facts.title: Nonentrant McIntyre eliminates Rhodes
facts.text: WWE explicitly assigns the outside-interference elimination to McIntyre.

facts.title: Reigns wins his second Royal Rumble
facts.text: Reigns last eliminated Gunther, adding to his2015 victory.

facts.title: Liv Morgan wins her first Royal Rumble
facts.text: Morgan last eliminated returning Stratton after two earlier runner-up finishes.

facts.title: Liv and Nattie continue all-event participation
facts.text: WWE identifies them as the only women to participate in all nine womens Royal Rumbles through2026.

facts.title: Bella Twins reunite in the Rumble
facts.text: Brie returned at29 and reunited with Nikki; WWE assigns Lyra to Brie and Bayley to Nikki.

facts.title: Alba Fyre intrudes without becoming an entrant
facts.text: Rhea threw out Chelsea companion Alba; this is a narrative incident, not a thirtieth elimination.

facts.title: Lash Legend leads elimination count
facts.text: Five official victims: Grace, Nikki, Brie, Charlotte and IYO.

facts.title: Bret Hart sets the Rumble's very first longevity record
facts.text: Entering as one of the two opening wrestlers, Bret Hart lasted 25 minutes 42 seconds before being eliminated by Don Muraco — establishing the inaugural Royal Rumble's longevity record in the very first-ever edition of the match, despite not winning.

facts.title: Jake Roberts scored the first-ever Royal Rumble elimination
facts.text: In the inaugural 1988 match, Jake "The Snake" Roberts tossed Butch Reed over the top rope for the very first elimination in Royal Rumble history.

facts.title: One Man Gang eliminated his own ally clearing Duggan's path to the win
facts.text: In the match's closing stretch, One Man Gang — trying to duck a Jim Duggan attack — accidentally eliminated his own tag partner/ally Dino Bravo instead, an own-goal elimination that helped open the door for Duggan to go on and win.

facts.title: One Man Gang led all eliminators with 4 — despite losing
facts.text: One Man Gang recorded the most eliminations of anyone in the 1988 match with four (B. Brian Blair, Jake Roberts, Hillbilly Jim, and finally his own ally Dino Bravo), the most of any participant that night, despite not winning himself.

facts.title: Duggan won the inaugural Rumble eight months after a career-threatening DUI arrest
facts.text: On May 26, 1987 — roughly eight months before he won the first-ever Royal Rumble — Jim Duggan was arrested for DUI in New Jersey alongside his on-screen rival The Iron Sheik; Duggan was found to be under the influence of marijuana and alcohol, Sheik tested positive for cocaine. The real-life incident briefly got Duggan released by the WWF before he was "ultimately brought back in a lower spot on the roster," from which he rebuilt to headline the inaugural Rumble.

facts.title: André the Giant's panic over a snake caused the match's only self-elimination
facts.text: After Jake Roberts had his boa constrictor "Damien" brought down to ringside, André the Giant reacted by climbing over the top rope and eliminating himself — the only self-elimination of the entire 1989 match.

facts.title: Jake Roberts becomes the first two-time Royal Rumble entrant
facts.text: Having competed in the inaugural 1988 Rumble, Jake Roberts's 1989 appearance made him the first wrestler ever to compete in two different Royal Rumble matches.

facts.title: Mr. Perfect breaks the one-year-old Rumble longevity record
facts.text: Mr. Perfect lasted 27 minutes 58 seconds before Hulk Hogan eliminated him, breaking Bret Hart's inaugural 25:42 longevity record from the year before — a record that would itself be broken again the very next year by Ted DiBiase's 44:47 at RR1990M.

facts.title: Ted DiBiase bought his way to a better draw via manager Slick
facts.text: In storyline, Ted DiBiase purchased his entry number from manager Slick to secure the coveted #30 (final) position in the 1989 match. The real-world framing of this as DiBiase gaming the draw process persisted into next year's event, where Wikipedia's 1990 recap explicitly calls him "Ted DiBiase, who had manipulated entry selections the previous year," prompting WWF president Jack Tunney to add "extra security" to the 1990 drawing.

facts.title: Tony Schiavone's final WWF PPV before jumping to WCW
facts.text: The 1990 Royal Rumble was the last WWF pay-per-view called by commentator Tony Schiavone before he left the company for World Championship Wrestling, where he became a lead announcer through the Monday Night Wars era; Gorilla Monsoon resumed lead commentary duties starting with WrestleMania VI.

facts.title: Ted DiBiase breaks Mr. Perfect's one-year-old longevity record
facts.text: Ted DiBiase lasted 44 minutes 47 seconds before being clotheslined out by Ultimate Warrior, shattering Mr. Perfect's 27:58 mark from the previous year's Rumble.

facts.title: Hogan and Warrior's big first face-off fizzled into a non-spot
facts.text: When reigning WWF Champion Hulk Hogan and Intercontinental Champion Ultimate Warrior finally squared off mid-match — a moment billed as historic since both champions were in the ring together for the first time — the pair simply bounced off the ropes and collided into one another without either man budging or falling, an anticlimactic beat before both moved on to other opponents.

facts.title: Big Boss Man's last Rumble as a villain
facts.text: RR1990M was Big Boss Man's final Royal Rumble/pay-per-view appearance as a heel; shortly afterward he refused to help Ted DiBiase in DiBiase's feud with Jake Roberts, fired manager Slick, and aligned himself with Hulk Hogan — completing his face turn.

facts.title: Yokozuna led all eliminators in the match he went on to win
facts.text: Yokozuna recorded 7 eliminations in the 1993 Royal Rumble — the most of any competitor in that match — on his way to winning the whole thing.

facts.title: Bob Backlund logged the longest individual time of the 1993 match
facts.text: Bob Backlund's individual survival time of 61 minutes 16 seconds was the longest of any competitor in the 1993 Royal Rumble.

facts.title: The only co-winners in Royal Rumble history
facts.text: Bret Hart and Lex Luger went over the top rope simultaneously in the match's final spot and were both declared winners — the first (and to date only) tie/co-win in Royal Rumble history. Both men were awarded WWF Championship title shots at WrestleMania X as a result.

facts.title: Diesel and Lex Luger tie for most eliminations in the match
facts.text: Diesel and Lex Luger each recorded 7 eliminations in the 1994 Royal Rumble, tying for the match's high — notably, Luger's own 7 eliminations came in the same match he'd go on to (jointly) win.

facts.title: Shawn Michaels becomes the first wrestler to win from the #1 draw
facts.text: Shawn Michaels won the 1995 Royal Rumble having entered at #1 — the first time in the event's eight-year history (1988–1995) that the wrestler who drew the opening spot went on to win the match.

facts.title: Mo and Owen Hart tie for the shortest survival time in the match
facts.text: Mo (of Men on a Mission) and Owen Hart each recorded the shortest individual survival time in the 1995 Royal Rumble, both lasting just 4 seconds.

facts.title: Bigelow expected for the Rumble, never appeared
facts.text: Bam Bam Bigelow was widely expected to be part of the 1996 Rumble build coming off 1995, but he did not appear on the card. Sources disagree on why: one account ties it to backstage friction with Shawn Michaels and the Kliq (he left for ECW shortly after), while another says he needed elbow surgery and that his last match before the gap was at Survivor Series 1995.

facts.title: Sabu considered for a spot, but Heyman steered him away
facts.text: Sabu was reportedly in the mix for a 1996 Rumble appearance, but Paul Heyman discouraged him from taking it in order to protect ECW's "outlaw" promotional image at the time.

facts.title: First Rumble to give every entrant their own entrance music
